verses.sanskrit: उशन् ह वै वाजश्रवसः सर्ववेदसं ददौ | तस्य ह नचिकेता नाम पुत्र आस ||
verses.transliteration: uśan ha vai vājaśravasaḥ sarvavedasaṃ dadau | tasya ha naciketā nāma putra āsa ||
verses.translation: Desiring the fruit (of sacrifice), Vājaśravas gave away all his possessions. He had a son named Naciketas.
verses.hindi: फल की कामना से वाजश्रवस् ने अपनी सारी सम्पत्ति दान कर दी। उनके पुत्र का नाम नचिकेता था।
verses.commentary: The setting. A father performs the Viśvajit sacrifice, in which the donor must give away everything. The motive is not pure — 'uśan' (desiring) hints at attachment to the result.
verses.wordMeaning: The setting. A father performs the Viśvajit sacrifice, in which the donor must give away everything. The motive is not pure — 'uśan' (desiring) hints at attachment to the result.

verses.sanskrit: तं ह कुमारं सन्तं दक्षिणासु नीयमानासु श्रद्धाविवेश सोऽमन्यत ||
verses.transliteration: taṃ ha kumāraṃ santaṃ dakṣiṇāsu nīyamānāsu śraddhāviveśa so'manyata ||
verses.translation: Though only a boy, faith entered him as the offerings were being led away. He thought:
verses.hindi: बालक होते हुए भी जब दक्षिणाएँ ले जाई जा रही थीं, उसमें श्रद्धा प्रविष्ट हुई। उसने सोचा —
verses.commentary: The decisive entry of śraddhā — faith, conviction, seriousness — into a child. Faith comes uninvited, even to the young; it is its own qualification.
verses.wordMeaning: The decisive entry of śraddhā — faith, conviction, seriousness — into a child. Faith comes uninvited, even to the young; it is its own qualification.

verses.sanskrit: पीतोदका जग्धतृणा दुग्धदोहा निरिन्द्रियाः | अनन्दा नाम ते लोकास्तान् स गच्छति ता ददत् ||
verses.transliteration: pītodakā jagdhatṛṇā dugdhadohā nirindriyāḥ | anandā nāma te lokāstān sa gacchati tā dadat ||
verses.translation: 'Those cows have drunk their last water, eaten their last grass, given their last milk, and have no senses left. Joyless are the worlds the giver of these reaches.'
verses.hindi: "जिन गायों ने अन्तिम जल पी लिया, अन्तिम तृण खा लिया, अन्तिम दूध दे दिया, इन्द्रियाँ क्षीण हो गईं — ऐसी गायों को दान करने वाला 'अनन्द' नामक लोकों को जाता है।"
verses.commentary: The boy's piercing critique. To give what is worn-out is not generosity but rejection. The 'worlds without joy' awaits such a giver.
verses.wordMeaning: The boy's piercing critique. To give what is worn-out is not generosity but rejection. The 'worlds without joy' awaits such a giver.

verses.sanskrit: स होवाच पितरं तत कस्मै मां दास्यसीति | द्वितीयं तृतीयं तं होवाच मृत्यवे त्वा ददामीति ||
verses.transliteration: sa hovāca pitaraṃ tata kasmai māṃ dāsyasīti | dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ taṃ hovāca mṛtyave tvā dadāmīti ||
verses.translation: He said to his father: 'Father, to whom will you give me?' A second and a third time he asked. The father said in anger: 'To Death I give you!'
verses.hindi: उसने पिता से पूछा — "पिता, आप मुझे किसको देंगे?" दूसरी, तीसरी बार पूछने पर पिता ने क्रोध में कहा — "मृत्यु को देता हूँ तुझे!"
verses.commentary: The boy's logical extension: if every possession must be given, what about me? Three times the question — the third triggers a fateful word.
verses.wordMeaning: The boy's logical extension: if every possession must be given, what about me? Three times the question — the third triggers a fateful word.

verses.sanskrit: बहूनामेमि प्रथमो बहूनामेमि मध्यमः | किं स्विद्यमस्य कर्तव्यं यन्मयाद्य करिष्यति ||
verses.transliteration: bahūnāmemi prathamo bahūnāmemi madhyamaḥ | kiṃ svidyamasya kartavyaṃ yanmayādya kariṣyati ||
verses.translation: (Naciketas reflects:) 'Among many I go first; among many I go in the middle. What duty of Yama's is there which he will accomplish through me today?'
verses.hindi: "बहुतों में मैं प्रथम (श्रेष्ठ) जाता हूँ; बहुतों में मध्य (मध्यम) जाता हूँ। मृत्यु का ऐसा कौन-सा कर्तव्य है जो आज मेरे द्वारा सिद्ध होगा?"
verses.commentary: The boy submits to his father's word without panic. He reflects: I am not the worst — what then is the purpose Yama wants from me? Curiosity, not fear, takes over.
verses.wordMeaning: The boy submits to his father's word without panic. He reflects: I am not the worst — what then is the purpose Yama wants from me? Curiosity, not fear, takes over.

verses.sanskrit: अनुपश्य यथा पूर्वे प्रतिपश्य तथापरे | सस्यमिव मर्त्यः पच्यते सस्यमिवाजायते पुनः ||
verses.transliteration: anupaśya yathā pūrve pratipaśya tathāpare | sasyamiva martyaḥ pacyate sasyamivājāyate punaḥ ||
verses.translation: (Naciketas to his father:) 'Look at how the ancestors went, look at those who came after. Like a stalk of grain a mortal ripens; like a stalk of grain he is born again.'
verses.hindi: "पूर्वजों को देखो, बाद वालों को देखो — मनुष्य धान्य की भाँति पकता है, और धान्य की भाँति फिर जन्म लेता है।"
verses.commentary: The boy consoles the father: do not be ashamed of your word. Look at the ancients — humans live and die like grain. The simile is humble and exact: ripen, harvest, regrow.
verses.wordMeaning: The boy consoles the father: do not be ashamed of your word. Look at the ancients — humans live and die like grain. The simile is humble and exact: ripen, harvest, regrow.

verses.sanskrit: वैश्वानरः प्रविशत्यतिथिर्ब्राह्मणो गृहान् | तस्यैतां शान्तिं कुर्वन्ति हर वैवस्वतोदकम् ||
verses.transliteration: vaiśvānaraḥ praviśatyatithirbrāhmaṇo gṛhān | tasyaitāṃ śāntiṃ kurvanti hara vaivasvatodakam ||
verses.translation: (Yama's servants:) 'A Brahmin guest enters a house like fire (Vaiśvānara). They pacify him thus: O Vaivasvata (Yama), bring water for him.'
verses.hindi: "ब्राह्मण अतिथि घर में वैश्वानर (अग्नि) की भाँति प्रवेश करता है। उसकी शान्ति के लिये जल लाओ, हे वैवस्वत!"
verses.commentary: The boy arrives at Yama's house — and Yama is away. The servants warn: a Brahmin-guest unattended is fire that burns the host. Bring water — the welcome-rite must be done.
verses.wordMeaning: The boy arrives at Yama's house — and Yama is away. The servants warn: a Brahmin-guest unattended is fire that burns the host. Bring water — the welcome-rite must be done.

verses.sanskrit: आशाप्रतीक्षे संगतं सूनृतां चेष्टापूर्ते पुत्रपशूंश्च सर्वान् | एतद्वृङ्क्ते पुरुषस्याल्पमेधसो यस्यानश्नन् वसति ब्राह्मणो गृहे ||
verses.transliteration: āśāpratīkṣe saṃgataṃ sūnṛtāṃ ceṣṭāpūrte putrapaśūṃśca sarvān | etadvṛṅkte puruṣasyālpamedhaso yasyānaśnan vasati brāhmaṇo gṛhe ||
verses.translation: 'Hope, expectation, companionship, gentle speech, sacrifices and good works, children and cattle — all these are taken away from the small-minded man in whose house a Brahmin dwells without food.'
verses.hindi: "आशा, प्रतीक्षा, संगत्व, सूनृत वाणी, इष्टापूर्त, पुत्र, पशु — ये सब उस अल्प-मति पुरुष से छिन जाते हैं जिसके घर में ब्राह्मण भोजन के बिना रहता है।"
verses.commentary: The catalog of losses for an unwelcoming host. The cost is not magical — it is the natural withering of a household whose order is broken.
verses.wordMeaning: The catalog of losses for an unwelcoming host. The cost is not magical — it is the natural withering of a household whose order is broken.

verses.sanskrit: तिस्रो रात्रीर्यदवात्सीर्गृहे मेऽनश्नन् ब्रह्मन्नतिथिर्नमस्यः | नमस्तेऽस्तु ब्रह्मन् स्वस्ति मेऽस्तु तस्मात्प्रति त्रीन् वरान् वृणीष्व ||
verses.transliteration: tisro rātrīryadavātsīrgṛhe me'naśnan brahmannatithirnamasyaḥ | namaste'stu brahman svasti me'stu tasmātprati trīn varān vṛṇīṣva ||
verses.translation: (Yama returns:) 'O Brahmin, you have lived in my house three nights without food — an honored guest. Salutations to you; may it be well with me. Therefore, ask three boons in return.'
verses.hindi: "हे ब्राह्मण! तू तीन रात्रि बिना भोजन के मेरे घर रहा — पूज्य अतिथि। तुझे नमस्कार; मेरा कल्याण हो। इसलिये तीन वर माँग।"
verses.commentary: Yama, deeply embarrassed, makes amends. Three nights of unmet welcome → three boons. The boy's calm presence has the power to rebalance even Death.
verses.wordMeaning: Yama, deeply embarrassed, makes amends. Three nights of unmet welcome → three boons. The boy's calm presence has the power to rebalance even Death.

verses.sanskrit: शान्तसङ्कल्पः सुमना यथा स्याद्वीतमन्युर्गौतमो माभि मृत्यो | त्वत्प्रसृष्टं माभिवदेत्प्रतीत एतत् त्रयाणां प्रथमं वरं वृणे ||
verses.transliteration: śāntasaṅkalpaḥ sumanā yathā syādvītamanyurgautamo mābhi mṛtyo | tvatprasṛṣṭaṃ mābhivadetpratīta etat trayāṇāṃ prathamaṃ varaṃ vṛṇe ||
verses.translation: (Naciketas:) 'O Death, let Gautama (my father) be tranquil-minded, well-disposed, free of anger toward me. Let him recognize me when sent back by you and speak with me. This is the first of the three boons I ask.'
verses.hindi: "हे मृत्यो! मेरा पिता गौतम शान्त-सङ्कल्प हो, प्रसन्न-मन हो, क्रोध-रहित हो। तेरे द्वारा भेजे जाने पर वह मुझे पहचाने और मुझसे प्रेम-पूर्वक बात करे। यह तीनों में से पहला वर मैं माँगता हूँ।"
verses.commentary: The first boon: not personal advantage, but reconciliation with the father. The boy chooses to repair what the father broke. Filial maturity at the highest level.
verses.wordMeaning: The first boon: not personal advantage, but reconciliation with the father. The boy chooses to repair what the father broke. Filial maturity at the highest level.

verses.sanskrit: यथा पुरस्ताद् भविता प्रतीत औद्दालकिरारुणिर्मत्प्रसृष्टः | सुखं रात्रीः शयिता वीतमन्युस्त्वां ददृशिवान्मृत्युमुखात् प्रमुक्तम् ||
verses.transliteration: yathā purastād bhavitā pratīta auddālakirāruṇirmatprasṛṣṭaḥ | sukhaṃ rātrīḥ śayitā vītamanyustvāṃ dadṛśivānmṛtyumukhāt pramuktam ||
verses.translation: (Yama:) 'As before, will Auddālaki Āruṇi (your father) be — recognizing you, sent back by me. He will sleep peacefully at nights, free of anger, seeing you released from Death's mouth.'
verses.hindi: "वैसा ही होगा जैसा पहले था — औद्दालकि आरुणि तुझे पहचानेगा, मेरे द्वारा भेजे जाने पर। वह क्रोध-रहित होकर रात्रियाँ सुख से सोयेगा — मृत्यु के मुख से छूटा हुआ तुझे देखकर।"
verses.commentary: Yama grants the first boon precisely. Note the rich human detail: 'sleep peacefully at nights' — the father's anguish over his careless word will be lifted. Grace runs through generations.
verses.wordMeaning: Yama grants the first boon precisely. Note the rich human detail: 'sleep peacefully at nights' — the father's anguish over his careless word will be lifted. Grace runs through generations.

verses.sanskrit: स्वर्गे लोके न भयं किञ्चनास्ति न तत्र त्वं न जरया बिभेति | उभे तीर्त्वाऽशनायापिपासे शोकातिगो मोदते स्वर्गलोके ||
verses.transliteration: svarge loke na bhayaṃ kiñcanāsti na tatra tvaṃ na jarayā bibheti | ubhe tīrtvā'śanāyāpipāse śokātigo modate svargaloke ||
verses.translation: (Naciketas:) 'In heaven there is no fear of any kind; you are not there, nor is age feared. Having crossed both hunger and thirst, beyond sorrow, one rejoices in heaven.'
verses.hindi: "स्वर्ग-लोक में कोई भय नहीं — वहाँ तुम नहीं हो, न जरा से डर है। भूख-प्यास दोनों को पार करके, शोक-रहित होकर, मनुष्य स्वर्ग में आनन्द भोगता है।"
verses.commentary: The boy describes heaven before asking about access. A precise definition: no fear, no death, no aging, no hunger, no thirst, no sorrow. The list defines what suffering is.
verses.wordMeaning: The boy describes heaven before asking about access. A precise definition: no fear, no death, no aging, no hunger, no thirst, no sorrow. The list defines what suffering is.

verses.sanskrit: स त्वमग्निं स्वर्ग्यमध्येषि मृत्यो प्रब्रूहि त्वं श्रद्दधानाय मह्यम् | स्वर्गलोका अमृतत्वं भजन्त एतद् द्वितीयेन वृणे वरेण ||
verses.transliteration: sa tvamagniṃ svargyamadhyeṣi mṛtyo prabrūhi tvaṃ śraddadhānāya mahyam | svargalokā amṛtatvaṃ bhajanta etad dvitīyena vṛṇe vareṇa ||
verses.translation: 'O Death, you know the fire that leads to heaven. Teach it to me — I am faithful. The heaven-dwellers attain immortality. This I ask as the second boon.'
verses.hindi: "हे मृत्यो! तू उस स्वर्ग्य अग्नि को जानता है। मुझे — श्रद्धावान् को — उसकी विधि सिखा। स्वर्ग-वासी अमरत्व प्राप्त करते हैं। यह मैं दूसरा वर माँगता हूँ।"
verses.commentary: The second boon: not heaven for myself, but the knowledge of the fire-rite (yajña) that leads there. The boy asks for transferable knowledge, not personal benefit.
verses.wordMeaning: The second boon: not heaven for myself, but the knowledge of the fire-rite (yajña) that leads there. The boy asks for transferable knowledge, not personal benefit.

verses.sanskrit: प्र ते ब्रवीमि तदु मे निबोध स्वर्ग्यमग्निं नचिकेतः प्रजानन् | अनन्तलोकाप्तिमथो प्रतिष्ठां विद्धि त्वमेतं निहितं गुहायाम् ||
verses.transliteration: pra te bravīmi tadu me nibodha svargyamagniṃ naciketaḥ prajānan | anantalokāptimatho pratiṣṭhāṃ viddhi tvametaṃ nihitaṃ guhāyām ||
verses.translation: (Yama:) 'I will tell you, Naciketas — listen well. I, the knower of the fire that leads to heaven. Know it as the attainment of the infinite world, as the foundation — hidden in the cave (of the heart).'
verses.hindi: "मैं तुझे बताता हूँ, हे नचिकेता, ध्यान दे — मैं स्वर्ग्य अग्नि का ज्ञाता हूँ। उसे जान — अनन्त लोक की प्राप्ति, और प्रतिष्ठा भी; हृदय-गुहा में निहित।"
verses.commentary: Yama agrees and locates the fire: it is not 'out there' alone — it is also hidden in the cave of the heart. The same fire that lights the outer altar is the inner foundation.
verses.wordMeaning: Yama agrees and locates the fire: it is not 'out there' alone — it is also hidden in the cave of the heart. The same fire that lights the outer altar is the inner foundation.

verses.sanskrit: लोकादिमग्निं तमुवाच तस्मै या इष्टका यावतीर्वा यथा वा | स चापि तत्प्रत्यवदद्यथोक्तमथास्य मृत्युः पुनरेवाह तुष्टः ||
verses.transliteration: lokādimagniṃ tamuvāca tasmai yā iṣṭakā yāvatīrvā yathā vā | sa cāpi tatpratyavadadyathoktamathāsya mṛtyuḥ punarevāha tuṣṭaḥ ||
verses.translation: Yama taught him the world-originating fire — what bricks, how many, how arranged. The boy repeated it back exactly. Then Death, pleased, spoke again.
verses.hindi: यम ने उसे लोक-आदि अग्नि का उपदेश दिया — कौन-सी इष्टकाएँ, कितनी, और किस क्रम में। नचिकेता ने ज्यों-का-त्यों दोहराया। तब प्रसन्न होकर मृत्यु फिर बोला।
verses.commentary: The teaching exchange is shown in miniature. The boy receives precise technical instruction and demonstrates perfect recall. Pleasure follows for the teacher.
verses.wordMeaning: The teaching exchange is shown in miniature. The boy receives precise technical instruction and demonstrates perfect recall. Pleasure follows for the teacher.

verses.sanskrit: तमब्रवीत् प्रीयमाणो महात्मा वरं तवेहाद्य ददामि भूयः | तवैव नाम्ना भविताऽयमग्निः सृङ्कां चेमामनेकरूपां गृहाण ||
verses.transliteration: tamabravīt prīyamāṇo mahātmā varaṃ tavehādya dadāmi bhūyaḥ | tavaiva nāmnā bhavitā'yamagniḥ sṛṅkāṃ cemāmanekarūpāṃ gṛhāṇa ||
verses.translation: Pleased, the great-souled (Yama) said: 'I give you yet another boon: this fire will be known by your very name. Accept also this many-formed garland (chain).'
verses.hindi: प्रसन्न होकर महात्मा (यम) ने कहा — "तुझे एक और वर देता हूँ: यह अग्नि तेरे ही नाम से जानी जायेगी। और यह अनेक रूपों वाली सृङ्का (माला) भी ग्रहण कर।"
verses.commentary: An unbidden bonus from the teacher: the fire-rite will bear the student's name forever (Nāciketa-agni), and a many-formed garland — symbol of the variety of forms knowledge takes.
verses.wordMeaning: An unbidden bonus from the teacher: the fire-rite will bear the student's name forever (Nāciketa-agni), and a many-formed garland — symbol of the variety of forms knowledge takes.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिणाचिकेतस्त्रिभिरेत्य सन्धिं त्रिकर्मकृत्तरति जन्ममृत्यू | ब्रह्मजज्ञं देवमीड्यं विदित्वा निचाय्येमां शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति ||
verses.transliteration: triṇāciketastribhiretya sandhiṃ trikarmakṛttarati janmamṛtyū | brahmajajñaṃ devamīḍyaṃ viditvā nicāyyemāṃ śāntimatyantameti ||
verses.translation: The 'thrice-Naciketas' — having joined with the three (mother, father, teacher), performing the three duties — crosses birth and death. Knowing the praiseworthy god born of Brahman, ever-seeing, he attains supreme peace.
verses.hindi: जो "त्रिणाचिकेत" है — तीन (माता-पिता-गुरु) के साथ संगत, तीन कर्म करने वाला — वह जन्म-मृत्यु को पार करता है। ब्रह्म से उत्पन्न पूज्य देव को जानकर, और निरन्तर देखकर, परम शान्ति प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: Praise of the perfected practitioner — one who has performed the Nāciketa-rite three times, while honoring his three relations and three duties (study, sacrifice, charity). Such a one crosses birth and death.
verses.wordMeaning: Praise of the perfected practitioner — one who has performed the Nāciketa-rite three times, while honoring his three relations and three duties (study, sacrifice, charity). Such a one crosses birth and death.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिणाचिकेतस्त्रयमेतद्विदित्वा य एवं विद्वांश्चिनुते नाचिकेतम् | स मृत्युपाशान् पुरतः प्रणोद्य शोकातिगो मोदते स्वर्गलोके ||
verses.transliteration: triṇāciketastrayametadviditvā ya evaṃ vidvāṃścinute nāciketam | sa mṛtyupāśān purataḥ praṇodya śokātigo modate svargaloke ||
verses.translation: He who, knowing the three (mother, father, teacher), thus learned, builds up the Nāciketa fire — pushing the noose of Death far away, beyond sorrow, rejoices in heaven.
verses.hindi: जो इन तीनों को जानकर — विद्वान् होकर — नाचिकेत अग्नि का चयन करता है, वह मृत्यु के पाशों को आगे से हटाकर, शोक-पार होकर, स्वर्ग में आनन्द भोगता है।
verses.commentary: Repetition with deepening: the same accomplishment is rephrased — death's noose pushed away, sorrow crossed, heavenly joy attained. Ritual fidelity has solid fruit.
verses.wordMeaning: Repetition with deepening: the same accomplishment is rephrased — death's noose pushed away, sorrow crossed, heavenly joy attained. Ritual fidelity has solid fruit.

verses.sanskrit: एष तेऽग्निर्नचिकेतः स्वर्ग्यो यमवृणीथा द्वितीयेन वरेण | एतमग्निं तवैव प्रवक्ष्यन्ति जनासस्तृतीयं वरं नचिकेतो वृणीष्व ||
verses.transliteration: eṣa te'gnirnaciketaḥ svargyo yamavṛṇīthā dvitīyena vareṇa | etamagniṃ tavaiva pravakṣyanti janāsastṛtīyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva ||
verses.translation: (Yama:) 'Naciketas, this is the heaven-leading fire which you chose as your second boon. People will speak of this fire by your name. Now, Naciketas, ask the third boon.'
verses.hindi: "हे नचिकेता! यही स्वर्ग्य अग्नि है जिसे तूने दूसरे वर में माँगा था। लोग इस अग्नि को तेरे नाम से ही पुकारेंगे। अब, हे नचिकेता, तीसरा वर माँग।"
verses.commentary: Yama formally confirms: second boon granted, fire named after the boy. Invitation to the third — which the verse setup is making clear will be momentous.
verses.wordMeaning: Yama formally confirms: second boon granted, fire named after the boy. Invitation to the third — which the verse setup is making clear will be momentous.

verses.sanskrit: येयं प्रेते विचिकित्सा मनुष्येऽस्तीत्येके नायमस्तीति चैके | एतद्विद्यामनुशिष्टस्त्वयाहं वराणामेष वरस्तृतीयः ||
verses.transliteration: yeyaṃ prete vicikitsā manuṣye'stītyeke nāyamastīti caike | etadvidyāmanuśiṣṭastvayāhaṃ varāṇāmeṣa varastṛtīyaḥ ||
verses.translation: 'There is this doubt about a man who has departed: some say he exists, others that he does not. I would learn this, taught by you. This is the third of the boons.'
verses.hindi: "मरे हुए मनुष्य के विषय में यह संशय है — कुछ कहते हैं वह "है", कुछ कहते हैं "नहीं है"। यही मैं तुमसे सीखना चाहता हूँ। यह तीनों में तीसरा वर है।"
verses.commentary: The eternal question, asked by a child to Death himself: does a person exist after death? Some say yes, some no. Naciketas asks not for theory but for direct instruction.
verses.wordMeaning: The eternal question, asked by a child to Death himself: does a person exist after death? Some say yes, some no. Naciketas asks not for theory but for direct instruction.

verses.sanskrit: देवैरत्रापि विचिकित्सितं पुरा न हि सुविज्ञेयमणुरेष धर्मः | अन्यं वरं नचिकेतो वृणीष्व मा मोपरोत्सीरति मा सृजैनम् ||
verses.transliteration: devairatrāpi vicikitsitaṃ purā na hi suvijñeyamaṇureṣa dharmaḥ | anyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva mā moparotsīrati mā sṛjainam ||
verses.translation: (Yama:) 'On this point even the gods of old had doubts. This is not easily known — the dharma is subtle. Ask another boon, Naciketas. Do not press me. Release me from this one.'
verses.hindi: "इस विषय में पुरातन देवों को भी संशय था; यह सुगमता से ज्ञेय नहीं है — यह धर्म अत्यन्त सूक्ष्म है। हे नचिकेता! दूसरा कोई वर माँग। मुझे मत बाँधो; इसे छोड़ दो।"
verses.commentary: Yama tries to deflect. Even the gods are unsure; the subject is too subtle; choose another boon. The teacher tests the student's resolve.
verses.wordMeaning: Yama tries to deflect. Even the gods are unsure; the subject is too subtle; choose another boon. The teacher tests the student's resolve.

verses.sanskrit: देवैरत्रापि विचिकित्सितं किल त्वं च मृत्यो यन्न सुज्ञेयमात्थ | वक्ता चास्य त्वादृगन्यो न लभ्यो नान्यो वरस्तुल्य एतस्य कश्चित् ||
verses.transliteration: devairatrāpi vicikitsitaṃ kila tvaṃ ca mṛtyo yanna sujñeyamāttha | vaktā cāsya tvādṛganyo na labhyo nānyo varastulya etasya kaścit ||
verses.translation: (Naciketas:) 'Even gods had doubts, you say; and you yourself say it is not easily known. But another teacher like you cannot be found. No other boon is equal to this.'
verses.hindi: "देवों को भी संशय था — तुम स्वयं कहते हो कि यह सुज्ञेय नहीं है। परन्तु तुम्हारे जैसा वक्ता कोई और नहीं मिलेगा; इसके समान दूसरा वर भी कोई नहीं।"
verses.commentary: The boy presses: the very difficulty of the question is why I need you to teach it. No other teacher; no other prize. Resolve at the highest pitch.
verses.wordMeaning: The boy presses: the very difficulty of the question is why I need you to teach it. No other teacher; no other prize. Resolve at the highest pitch.

verses.sanskrit: शतायुषः पुत्रपौत्रान् वृणीष्व बहून् पशून् हस्तिहिरण्यमश्वान् | भूमेर्महदायतनं वृणीष्व स्वयं च जीव शरदो यावदिच्छसि ||
verses.transliteration: śatāyuṣaḥ putrapautrān vṛṇīṣva bahūn paśūn hastihiraṇyamaśvān | bhūmermahadāyatanaṃ vṛṇīṣva svayaṃ ca jīva śarado yāvadicchasi ||
verses.translation: (Yama:) 'Ask for sons and grandsons of a hundred years; many cattle, elephants, gold, and horses. Ask for a great expanse of earth. Live yourself as many years as you wish.'
verses.hindi: "सौ वर्ष की आयु वाले पुत्र-पौत्र माँग; बहुत-से पशु, हाथी, सोना, और घोड़े। पृथ्वी का विशाल साम्राज्य माँग। और तू स्वयं भी जितने वर्ष जीना चाहे, जी।"
verses.commentary: The temptation. Yama offers everything a worldly heart could want: long-lived progeny, wealth, kingdom, longevity. Each item is precisely calibrated to appeal.
verses.wordMeaning: The temptation. Yama offers everything a worldly heart could want: long-lived progeny, wealth, kingdom, longevity. Each item is precisely calibrated to appeal.

verses.sanskrit: एतत्तुल्यं यदि मन्यसे वरं वृणीष्व वित्तं चिरजीविकां च | महाभूमौ नचिकेतस्त्वमेधि कामानां त्वा कामभाजं करोमि ||
verses.transliteration: etattulyaṃ yadi manyase varaṃ vṛṇīṣva vittaṃ cirajīvikāṃ ca | mahābhūmau naciketastvamedhi kāmānāṃ tvā kāmabhājaṃ karomi ||
verses.translation: 'If you think any boon is equal to (your question), ask it — wealth and long life. Be on the great earth, Naciketas; I will make you a master of all desires.'
verses.hindi: "यदि तू इसके समान कोई वर मानता है, तो उसे माँग — धन और दीर्घ जीवन। हे नचिकेता! बड़ी भूमि पर निवास कर — मैं तुझे सब कामनाओं का स्वामी बना दूँगा।"
verses.commentary: The escalation. Now Yama offers mastery over desires themselves — not merely the goods, but the power to fulfill any want. The most subtle bait of all.
verses.wordMeaning: The escalation. Now Yama offers mastery over desires themselves — not merely the goods, but the power to fulfill any want. The most subtle bait of all.

verses.sanskrit: ये ये कामा दुर्लभा मर्त्यलोके सर्वान् कामांश्छन्दतः प्रार्थयस्व | इमा रामाः सरथाः सतूर्या न हीदृशा लम्भनीया मनुष्यैः | आभिर्मत्प्रत्ताभिः परिचारयस्व नचिकेतो मरणं माऽनुप्राक्षीः ||
verses.transliteration: ye ye kāmā durlabhā martyaloke sarvān kāmāṃśchandataḥ prārthayasva | imā rāmāḥ sarathāḥ satūryā na hīdṛśā lambhanīyā manuṣyaiḥ | ābhirmatprattābhiḥ paricārayasva naciketo maraṇaṃ mā'nuprākṣīḥ ||
verses.translation: 'Whatever desires are hard to attain in the mortal world — ask all of them at will. These beauties with chariots and music — humans cannot obtain such. Be served by them, my gift. But, Naciketas, do not ask about death.'
verses.hindi: "मर्त्यलोक में जो भी कामनाएँ दुर्लभ हैं — सब अपनी इच्छा से माँग। ये अप्सराएँ, रथों और संगीत के साथ — मनुष्य ऐसी नहीं पा सकते। ये मेरी दी हुई हैं — इनसे सेवा करा। परन्तु, नचिकेता, मृत्यु के विषय में मत पूछ।"
verses.commentary: The most direct offer: cosmic-grade pleasure and beauty. And the explicit rule: not the death-question. Yama is testing absolutely.
verses.wordMeaning: The most direct offer: cosmic-grade pleasure and beauty. And the explicit rule: not the death-question. Yama is testing absolutely.

verses.sanskrit: श्वोभावा मर्त्यस्य यदन्तकैतत् सर्वेन्द्रियाणां जरयन्ति तेजः | अपि सर्वं जीवितमल्पमेव तवैव वाहास्तव नृत्यगीते ||
verses.transliteration: śvobhāvā martyasya yadantakaitat sarvendriyāṇāṃ jarayanti tejaḥ | api sarvaṃ jīvitamalpameva tavaiva vāhāstava nṛtyagīte ||
verses.translation: (Naciketas:) 'O Death, these things last only until tomorrow — they wear out the splendor of all senses. Even the longest life is short. Keep your chariots, your dance and song.'
verses.hindi: "हे अन्तक! ये कल तक रहने वाली हैं — इन्द्रियों के तेज को क्षीण करती हैं। पूरा जीवन ही अल्प है। तेरे रथ तेरे रहें, तेरे नृत्य-गीत भी।"
verses.commentary: The boy refuses, with biting precision: tomorrow-things, wearing the senses, short life. Three short reasons. Then: keep your gifts.
verses.wordMeaning: The boy refuses, with biting precision: tomorrow-things, wearing the senses, short life. Three short reasons. Then: keep your gifts.

verses.sanskrit: न वित्तेन तर्पणीयो मनुष्यो लप्स्यामहे वित्तमद्राक्ष्म चेत्त्वा | जीविष्यामो यावदीशिष्यसि त्वं वरस्तु मे वरणीयः स एव ||
verses.transliteration: na vittena tarpaṇīyo manuṣyo lapsyāmahe vittamadrākṣma cettvā | jīviṣyāmo yāvadīśiṣyasi tvaṃ varastu me varaṇīyaḥ sa eva ||
verses.translation: 'A man cannot be satisfied by wealth. Shall I get wealth merely because I have seen you? I will live only as long as you let me. The boon I want is the one already named.'
verses.hindi: "मनुष्य को धन से तृप्ति नहीं होती। तुझे देखकर क्या मैं धन प्राप्त कर लूँगा? मैं उतना ही जीऊँगा जितना तू रहने देगा। मेरा माँगा हुआ वर वही है।"
verses.commentary: Three blistering refutations. (1) Wealth cannot satisfy. (2) Even mortal life is in your hands. (3) The boon I asked for stands. Iron resolve.
verses.wordMeaning: Three blistering refutations. (1) Wealth cannot satisfy. (2) Even mortal life is in your hands. (3) The boon I asked for stands. Iron resolve.

verses.sanskrit: अजीर्यताममृतानामुपेत्य जीर्यन् मर्त्यः क्वधःस्थः प्रजानन् | अभिध्यायन् वर्णरतिप्रमोदानतिदीर्घे जीविते को रमेत ||
verses.transliteration: ajīryatāmamṛtānāmupetya jīryan martyaḥ kvadhaḥsthaḥ prajānan | abhidhyāyan varṇaratipramodānatidīrghe jīvite ko rameta ||
verses.translation: 'Having approached the undecaying immortals, what perishing mortal — knowing what he knows — would delight in a long life of pleasures, color, and joys?'
verses.hindi: "अजर अमरों के पास पहुँचकर, जरा-शील मर्त्य — जानने वाला — पता है निम्न पद पर बैठा — रंग, रति, और प्रमोद के विचार में पड़कर अति-दीर्घ जीवन में कौन रमेगा?"
verses.commentary: The decisive question. Having met the deathless, who would settle for mortal pleasures? The boy throws Yama's own ontology back at him.
verses.wordMeaning: The decisive question. Having met the deathless, who would settle for mortal pleasures? The boy throws Yama's own ontology back at him.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मिन्निदं विचिकित्सन्ति मृत्यो यत् साम्पराये महति ब्रूहि नस्तत् | योऽयं वरो गूढमनुप्रविष्टो नान्यं तस्मान्नचिकेता वृणीते ||
verses.transliteration: yasminnidaṃ vicikitsanti mṛtyo yat sāmparāye mahati brūhi nastat | yo'yaṃ varo gūḍhamanupraviṣṭo nānyaṃ tasmānnaciketā vṛṇīte ||
verses.translation: 'O Death, tell us about that great after-life concerning which men are in doubt. This is the boon — entering into the hidden. Naciketas chooses no other.'
verses.hindi: "हे मृत्यो! उस महान् साम्पराय (मृत्यु के बाद की स्थिति) के विषय में जिसमें लोगों को संशय है — हमें वही बता। यही वर है — जो छिपे हुए में प्रवेश करता है। नचिकेता दूसरा नहीं माँगता।"
verses.commentary: Closing of Vallī 1. The boy holds his ground. The boon must be the one that enters into the hidden — no other will satisfy. Yama must now teach.
verses.wordMeaning: Closing of Vallī 1. The boy holds his ground. The boon must be the one that enters into the hidden — no other will satisfy. Yama must now teach.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यच्छ्रेयोऽन्यदुतैव प्रेयस्ते उभे नानार्थे पुरुषं सिनीतः | तयोः श्रेय आददानस्य साधु भवति हीयतेऽर्थाद्य उ प्रेयो वृणीते ||
verses.transliteration: anyacchreyo'nyadutaiva preyaste ubhe nānārthe puruṣaṃ sinītaḥ | tayoḥ śreya ādadānasya sādhu bhavati hīyate'rthādya u preyo vṛṇīte ||
verses.translation: The good is one thing; the pleasant is another. These two, with different aims, bind a person. Of these, well it goes for the one who takes up the good; he who chooses the pleasant falls short of the goal.
verses.hindi: श्रेय (जो वास्तव में हितकर है) और प्रेय (जो प्रिय लगता है) — दोनों भिन्न अर्थ वाले हैं और मनुष्य को बाँधते हैं। श्रेय को अपनाने वाले का कल्याण होता है; जो प्रेय चुनता है, वह लक्ष्य से चूक जाता है।
verses.commentary: Life constantly offers two paths: what feels good (preya) and what is genuinely good (śreya). Most unconsciously follow preya their whole lives. The wise learn to choose śreya consistently — even when difficult.
verses.wordMeaning: Life constantly offers two paths: what feels good (preya) and what is genuinely good (śreya). Most unconsciously follow preya their whole lives. The wise learn to choose śreya consistently — even when difficult.

verses.sanskrit: श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतस्तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः | श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभि प्रेयसो वृणीते प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते ||
verses.transliteration: śreyaśca preyaśca manuṣyametastau samparītya vivinakti dhīraḥ | śreyo hi dhīro'bhi preyaso vṛṇīte preyo mando yogakṣemādvṛṇīte ||
verses.translation: The good and the pleasant approach a man. The wise one, examining both, discriminates between them. He chooses the good over the pleasant. The dull-witted, for the sake of comfort and security, chooses the pleasant.
verses.hindi: श्रेय और प्रेय — दोनों मनुष्य के पास आते हैं। धीर पुरुष दोनों की भली-भाँति परीक्षा करके विवेक करता है; वह प्रेय की अपेक्षा श्रेय को चुनता है। मन्द-बुद्धि — योग-क्षेम (आराम और सुरक्षा) के लिये — प्रेय को चुनता है।
verses.commentary: The faculty of viveka (discrimination) is what distinguishes wisdom from dullness. Both options arrive at every door; only the wise pause to examine before choosing.
verses.wordMeaning: The faculty of viveka (discrimination) is what distinguishes wisdom from dullness. Both options arrive at every door; only the wise pause to examine before choosing.

verses.sanskrit: स त्वं प्रियान् प्रियरूपांश्च कामानभिध्यायन् नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः | नैतां सृङ्कां वित्तमयीमवाप्तो यस्यां मज्जन्ति बहवो मनुष्याः ||
verses.transliteration: sa tvaṃ priyān priyarūpāṃśca kāmānabhidhyāyan naciketo'tyasrākṣīḥ | naitāṃ sṛṅkāṃ vittamayīmavāpto yasyāṃ majjanti bahavo manuṣyāḥ ||
verses.translation: You, Naciketas, examining the desirable and the seemingly-desirable, have rejected them. You did not accept that wealth-garland in which many men drown.
verses.hindi: हे नचिकेता! तूने प्रिय और प्रिय-रूप कामनाओं पर विचार करके उन्हें त्याग दिया। तूने उस धन-माला को नहीं स्वीकार किया जिसमें बहुत-से मनुष्य डूब जाते हैं।
verses.commentary: Yama's first praise. The boy passed the test: he saw through the gleam of wealth and refused. 'Drown' is the precise image — wealth pulls under those who clutch at it.
verses.wordMeaning: Yama's first praise. The boy passed the test: he saw through the gleam of wealth and refused. 'Drown' is the precise image — wealth pulls under those who clutch at it.

verses.sanskrit: दूरमेते विपरीते विषूची अविद्या या च विद्येति ज्ञाता | विद्याभीप्सिनं नचिकेतसं मन्ये न त्वा कामा बहवोऽलोलुपन्त ||
verses.transliteration: dūramete viparīte viṣūcī avidyā yā ca vidyeti jñātā | vidyābhīpsinaṃ naciketasaṃ manye na tvā kāmā bahavo'lolupanta ||
verses.translation: These two — known as ignorance and knowledge — are far apart, opposite, leading in different directions. I consider Naciketas a seeker of knowledge: many desires did not seduce you.
verses.hindi: अविद्या और विद्या — ये दोनों दूर-दूर, परस्पर विपरीत, भिन्न दिशाओं में जाने वाली हैं। मैं नचिकेता को विद्या का इच्छुक मानता हूँ — अनेक कामनाएँ तुझे लुब्ध नहीं कर सकीं।
verses.commentary: Knowledge and ignorance run in opposite directions. The same person cannot follow both. The boy's refusal of bait proves he is bound for knowledge.
verses.wordMeaning: Knowledge and ignorance run in opposite directions. The same person cannot follow both. The boy's refusal of bait proves he is bound for knowledge.

verses.sanskrit: अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः स्वयं धीराः पण्डितंमन्यमानाः | दन्द्रम्यमाणाः परियन्ति मूढा अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः ||
verses.transliteration: avidyāyāmantare vartamānāḥ svayaṃ dhīrāḥ paṇḍitaṃmanyamānāḥ | dandramyamāṇāḥ pariyanti mūḍhā andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ ||
verses.translation: Living in the midst of ignorance, considering themselves wise and learned, the deluded wander, struck again and again — like blind men led by the blind.
verses.hindi: अविद्या में रहते हुए स्वयं को धीर और पण्डित मानने वाले — ये मूढ़ बारम्बार ठोकर खाते भटकते हैं — जैसे अन्धों के द्वारा ले जाये जाने वाले अन्धे।
verses.commentary: The blind-leading-the-blind image (also in Mundaka). Confidence without insight is doubly dangerous: it misleads the confident and those who trust them.
verses.wordMeaning: The blind-leading-the-blind image (also in Mundaka). Confidence without insight is doubly dangerous: it misleads the confident and those who trust them.

verses.sanskrit: न साम्परायः प्रतिभाति बालं प्रमाद्यन्तं वित्तमोहेन मूढम् | अयं लोको नास्ति पर इति मानी पुनः पुनर्वशमापद्यते मे ||
verses.transliteration: na sāmparāyaḥ pratibhāti bālaṃ pramādyantaṃ vittamohena mūḍham | ayaṃ loko nāsti para iti mānī punaḥ punarvaśamāpadyate me ||
verses.translation: The afterlife does not appear to the careless, foolish child deluded by wealth. He who thinks 'this world exists, no other' — again and again falls into my power.
verses.hindi: धन-मोह से मूढ़, प्रमादी बाल-बुद्धि को पर-लोक नहीं दिखता। "केवल यह लोक है, कोई दूसरा नहीं" — ऐसा मानने वाला बार-बार मेरे (मृत्यु के) वश में पड़ता है।
verses.commentary: Yama identifies his own most reliable clients: the materialist who denies any deeper reality. Such a one returns to him again and again. Denial of the transcendent is the bondage of repeated death.
verses.wordMeaning: Yama identifies his own most reliable clients: the materialist who denies any deeper reality. Such a one returns to him again and again. Denial of the transcendent is the bondage of repeated death.

verses.sanskrit: श्रवणायापि बहुभिर्यो न लभ्यः शृण्वन्तोऽपि बहवो यं न विद्युः | आश्चर्यो वक्ता कुशलोऽस्य लब्धाश्चर्यो ज्ञाता कुशलानुशिष्टः ||
verses.transliteration: śravaṇāyāpi bahubhiryo na labhyaḥ śṛṇvanto'pi bahavo yaṃ na vidyuḥ | āścaryo vaktā kuśalo'sya labdhāścaryo jñātā kuśalānuśiṣṭaḥ ||
verses.translation: He whom many cannot even hear of; whom, hearing, many do not understand — wonderful is the teacher of him; skillful the receiver; wonderful is the knower, taught by the skillful.
verses.hindi: जिसके विषय में बहुत-से सुन भी नहीं पाते; जिसे सुनकर भी बहुत-से नहीं समझ पाते — उसका वक्ता आश्चर्यकर है, और कुशल है उसका प्राप्तकर्ता; आश्चर्य ही है उसका ज्ञाता, जिसे कुशल गुरु ने सिखाया।
verses.commentary: Three rarities. (1) Even hearing of the Self is rare. (2) Among hearers, the one who understands is rare. (3) Among understanders, the one who knows is rare. Each level of rarity multiplies.
verses.wordMeaning: Three rarities. (1) Even hearing of the Self is rare. (2) Among hearers, the one who understands is rare. (3) Among understanders, the one who knows is rare. Each level of rarity multiplies.

verses.sanskrit: न नरेणावरेण प्रोक्त एष सुविज्ञेयो बहुधा चिन्त्यमानः | अनन्यप्रोक्ते गतिरत्र नास्त्यणीयान् ह्यतर्क्यमणुप्रमाणात् ||
verses.transliteration: na nareṇāvareṇa prokta eṣa suvijñeyo bahudhā cintyamānaḥ | ananyaprokte gatiratra nāstyaṇīyān hyatarkyamaṇupramāṇāt ||
verses.translation: Taught by a lesser man, this is not well known, though pondered in many ways. Without one who is non-different (from Brahman) teaching, there is no way — for it is finer than the atom, beyond reasoning.
verses.hindi: अवर (साधारण) पुरुष द्वारा कहा गया — चाहे अनेक प्रकार से चिन्तन किया जाये — यह सुगमता से ज्ञात नहीं होता। अनन्य (ब्रह्म से अभिन्न) के बिना कहा गया — कोई मार्ग नहीं — क्योंकि यह अणु से भी सूक्ष्म, तर्क से परे है।
verses.commentary: The crucial requirement of teacher-quality. The Self cannot be taught by 'an ordinary man' — only by one who is 'non-different' (anan­ya) from Brahman. Knowledge by acquaintance must come from one already acquainted.
verses.wordMeaning: The crucial requirement of teacher-quality. The Self cannot be taught by 'an ordinary man' — only by one who is 'non-different' (anan­ya) from Brahman. Knowledge by acquaintance must come from one already acquainted.

verses.sanskrit: नैषा तर्केण मतिरापनेया प्रोक्ताऽन्येनैव सुज्ञानाय प्रेष्ठ | यां त्वमापः सत्यधृतिर्बतासि त्वादृङ् नो भूयान्नचिकेतः प्रष्टा ||
verses.transliteration: naiṣā tarkeṇa matirāpaneyā proktā'nyenaiva sujñānāya preṣṭha | yāṃ tvamāpaḥ satyadhṛtirbatāsi tvādṛṅ no bhūyānnaciketaḥ praṣṭā ||
verses.translation: This understanding cannot be reached by reasoning. Taught by another (an immediate knower), it is then easily known. You have reached it, dear one — you of true resolve. May we have many questioners like you, Naciketas!
verses.hindi: यह बुद्धि तर्क से प्राप्य नहीं — किसी अन्य (अनुभवी ज्ञाता) के द्वारा कही जाने पर ही सुगम होती है। तूने इसे प्राप्त किया है, हे प्रिय — तू सत्य-धृति वाला है। हे नचिकेता! तेरे जैसा प्रश्न-कर्ता हमें बहुत मिले।
verses.commentary: Yama compliments the boy openly: rare student, true resolve. The compliment is also a structural teaching: the Self cannot be reasoned into; it must be 'caught' from one who has it.
verses.wordMeaning: Yama compliments the boy openly: rare student, true resolve. The compliment is also a structural teaching: the Self cannot be reasoned into; it must be 'caught' from one who has it.

verses.sanskrit: जानाम्यहं शेवधिरित्यनित्यं न ह्यध्रुवैः प्राप्यते हि ध्रुवं तत् | ततो मया नाचिकेतश्चितोऽग्निरनित्यैर्द्रव्यैः प्राप्तवानस्मि नित्यम् ||
verses.transliteration: jānāmyahaṃ śevadhirityanityaṃ na hyadhruvaiḥ prāpyate hi dhruvaṃ tat | tato mayā nāciketaścito'gniranityairdravyaiḥ prāptavānasmi nityam ||
verses.translation: (Yama:) 'I know: the treasure (of heaven) is impermanent — for the eternal is not gained by the non-eternal. Therefore I built the Nāciketa fire with impermanent things and gained the eternal.'
verses.hindi: "मैं जानता हूँ — शेवधि (स्वर्ग-कोष) अनित्य है; क्योंकि अध्रुव (अनित्य) से ध्रुव (नित्य) नहीं मिलता। इसलिये मैंने अनित्य द्रव्यों से नाचिकेत-अग्नि का चयन किया, और नित्य को प्राप्त किया।"
verses.commentary: Yama's autobiography. He explains: even my own divine station, built from rites, is impermanent — but the eternal can still be approached through it. Method and goal are not the same level.
verses.wordMeaning: Yama's autobiography. He explains: even my own divine station, built from rites, is impermanent — but the eternal can still be approached through it. Method and goal are not the same level.

verses.sanskrit: कामस्याप्तिं जगतः प्रतिष्ठां क्रतोरानन्त्यमभयस्य पारम् | स्तोममहदुरुगायं प्रतिष्ठां दृष्ट्वा धृत्या धीरो नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः ||
verses.transliteration: kāmasyāptiṃ jagataḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ kratorānantyamabhayasya pāram | stomamahadurugāyaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhṛtyā dhīro naciketo'tyasrākṣīḥ ||
verses.translation: The fulfillment of desire, the foundation of the world, the infinite fruit of sacrifice, the further shore of fearlessness, the greatly praised wide-going abode — seeing this, you, wise Naciketas, with steadiness, rejected it!
verses.hindi: कामना की पूर्ति, जगत् की प्रतिष्ठा, यज्ञ का अनन्त फल, अभय का पार, स्तुत-योग्य महान् उरुगाय प्रतिष्ठा — इन सबको देखकर भी, हे धीर नचिकेता! तूने धैर्य से अस्वीकार कर दिया।
verses.commentary: Yama enumerates everything the worldly heart could want, and marvels: you saw it and refused it. The praise is meant to make the boy fully aware of what he has chosen against.
verses.wordMeaning: Yama enumerates everything the worldly heart could want, and marvels: you saw it and refused it. The praise is meant to make the boy fully aware of what he has chosen against.

verses.sanskrit: तं दुर्दर्शं गूढमनुप्रविष्टं गुहाहितं गह्वरेष्ठं पुराणम् | अध्यात्मयोगाधिगमेन देवं मत्वा धीरो हर्षशोकौ जहाति ||
verses.transliteration: taṃ durdarśaṃ gūḍhamanupraviṣṭaṃ guhāhitaṃ gahvareṣṭhaṃ purāṇam | adhyātmayogādhigamena devaṃ matvā dhīro harṣaśokau jahāti ||
verses.translation: Hard to see, deeply hidden, set in the cave, abiding in the depth, primordial — knowing him through inward yoga, the wise one leaves joy and sorrow behind.
verses.hindi: दुर्दर्श, गूढ़ रूप से प्रविष्ट, हृदय-गुहा में स्थित, गहरे में निवास करने वाला, पुराण — उस देव को अध्यात्म-योग से जानकर धीर पुरुष हर्ष और शोक को त्याग देता है।
verses.commentary: Five qualifications of the Self: hard to see, deeply hidden, in the cave, in the depths, primordial. Adhyātma-yoga (inward yoga) — not study — is the path. The fruit: equanimity beyond joy and sorrow.
verses.wordMeaning: Five qualifications of the Self: hard to see, deeply hidden, in the cave, in the depths, primordial. Adhyātma-yoga (inward yoga) — not study — is the path. The fruit: equanimity beyond joy and sorrow.

verses.sanskrit: एतच्छ्रुत्वा सम्परिगृह्य मर्त्यः प्रवृह्य धर्म्यमणुमेतमाप्य | स मोदते मोदनीयं हि लब्ध्वा विवृतं सद्म नचिकेतसं मन्ये ||
verses.transliteration: etacchrutvā samparigṛhya martyaḥ pravṛhya dharmyamaṇumetamāpya | sa modate modanīyaṃ hi labdhvā vivṛtaṃ sadma naciketasaṃ manye ||
verses.translation: Having heard this, embraced it, taken hold of the dharma — having attained this subtle one — a mortal rejoices, for he has gained what is worthy of rejoicing. I think the abode is wide open for Naciketas.
verses.hindi: इसको सुनकर, ग्रहण करके, धर्म रूप अणु को अलग करके, उसे प्राप्त करके — मनुष्य आनन्दित होता है; क्योंकि उसने आनन्दनीय को पाया है। मैं समझता हूँ कि नचिकेता के लिये वह सद्म (ब्रह्म-धाम) खुला है।
verses.commentary: Yama foretells the boy's success. The five-step path: hear → embrace → grasp the dharma → attain the subtle → rejoice. The abode of Brahman stands open.
verses.wordMeaning: Yama foretells the boy's success. The five-step path: hear → embrace → grasp the dharma → attain the subtle → rejoice. The abode of Brahman stands open.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यत्र धर्मादन्यत्राधर्मादन्यत्रास्मात्कृताकृतात् | अन्यत्र भूताच्च भव्याच्च यत्तत्पश्यसि तद्वद ||
verses.transliteration: anyatra dharmādanyatrādharmādanyatrāsmātkṛtākṛtāt | anyatra bhūtācca bhavyācca yattatpaśyasi tadvada ||
verses.translation: (Naciketas:) 'That which is other than dharma and other than adharma, other than the done and the undone, other than what has been and what will be — tell me what you see of that.'
verses.hindi: "जो धर्म से अन्य, अधर्म से अन्य, कृत-अकृत से अन्य, भूत-भव्य से अन्य है — जो तू देखता है, वह मुझे बता।"
verses.commentary: Pivotal verse. The boy asks not for ethical or temporal categories but for what is beyond all binaries: good/bad, done/undone, past/future. He is asking for the absolute substrate.
verses.wordMeaning: Pivotal verse. The boy asks not for ethical or temporal categories but for what is beyond all binaries: good/bad, done/undone, past/future. He is asking for the absolute substrate.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वे वेदा यत्पदमामनन्ति तपांसि सर्वाणि च यद्वदन्ति | यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति तत्ते पदं सङ्ग्रहेण ब्रवीम्योमित्येतत् ||
verses.transliteration: sarve vedā yatpadamāmananti tapāṃsi sarvāṇi ca yadvadanti | yadicchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti tatte padaṃ saṅgraheṇa bravīmyomityetat ||
verses.translation: (Yama:) 'That abode which all the Vedas extol, which all austerities declare, desiring which men practice celibacy — that abode I declare to you in brief: it is OM.'
verses.hindi: "जिस पद को सब वेद कहते हैं, जिसे सब तप घोषित करते हैं, जिसकी इच्छा से मनुष्य ब्रह्मचर्य का पालन करते हैं — वह पद मैं तुझे संक्षेप में बताता हूँ — वह "ॐ" है।"
verses.commentary: Yama gives the answer in one syllable: OM. The aim of all Vedas, austerities, and continence — encapsulated in three sounds.
verses.wordMeaning: Yama gives the answer in one syllable: OM. The aim of all Vedas, austerities, and continence — encapsulated in three sounds.

verses.sanskrit: एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं ब्रह्म एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं परम् | एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं ज्ञात्वा यो यदिच्छति तस्य तत् ||
verses.transliteration: etaddhyevākṣaraṃ brahma etaddhyevākṣaraṃ param | etaddhyevākṣaraṃ jñātvā yo yadicchati tasya tat ||
verses.translation: This syllable is verily Brahman; this syllable is verily the highest. Knowing this syllable, whatever one desires — that is his.
verses.hindi: यही अक्षर ब्रह्म है; यही अक्षर परम है। इसी अक्षर को जानकर, जो जिसकी इच्छा करता है — वह उसे प्राप्त होता है।
verses.commentary: OM is identified with Brahman both relative and absolute. The fruit of knowing it: 'whatever one wishes' — both worldly and transcendent. The single syllable is omnivalent.
verses.wordMeaning: OM is identified with Brahman both relative and absolute. The fruit of knowing it: 'whatever one wishes' — both worldly and transcendent. The single syllable is omnivalent.

verses.sanskrit: एतदालम्बनं श्रेष्ठमेतदालम्बनं परम् | एतदालम्बनं ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ||
verses.transliteration: etadālambanaṃ śreṣṭhametadālambanaṃ param | etadālambanaṃ jñātvā brahmaloke mahīyate ||
verses.translation: This support is the highest; this support is the supreme. Knowing this support, one is exalted in the world of Brahman.
verses.hindi: यही आलम्बन (आश्रय) श्रेष्ठ है; यही परम। इसी आलम्बन को जानकर मनुष्य ब्रह्म-लोक में महिमा को प्राप्त होता है।
verses.commentary: OM is named ālambana — the support. When the mind has nothing else to hold onto, it can hold onto OM. From that support it cannot fall.
verses.wordMeaning: OM is named ālambana — the support. When the mind has nothing else to hold onto, it can hold onto OM. From that support it cannot fall.

verses.sanskrit: न जायते म्रियते वा विपश्चिन्नायं कुतश्चिन्न बभूव कश्चित् | अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ||
verses.transliteration: na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścinnāyaṃ kutaścinna babhūva kaścit | ajo nityaḥ śāśvato'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre ||
verses.translation: The wise (Self) is not born and does not die. He has not come from anywhere; nothing has come from him. Unborn, eternal, everlasting, primordial — he is not killed when the body is killed.
verses.hindi: विपश्चित् (आत्मा) न जन्म लेता है, न मरता है। न वह किसी से आया है, न कोई उससे उत्पन्न हुआ। वह अज, नित्य, शाश्वत, पुराण है; शरीर के मारे जाने पर भी वह नहीं मारा जाता।
verses.commentary: The decisive verse on the Self's deathlessness. The Self is not born — therefore cannot die. It does not come from elsewhere — therefore cannot return there. Body and Self are categorically different.
verses.wordMeaning: The decisive verse on the Self's deathlessness. The Self is not born — therefore cannot die. It does not come from elsewhere — therefore cannot return there. Body and Self are categorically different.

verses.sanskrit: हन्ता चेन्मन्यते हन्तुं हतश्चेन्मन्यते हतम् | उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ||
verses.transliteration: hantā cenmanyate hantuṃ hataścenmanyate hatam | ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate ||
verses.translation: If the killer thinks he kills, and the killed thinks he is killed — both do not understand. This (Self) neither kills nor is killed.
verses.hindi: यदि मारने वाला सोचे "मैंने मारा", और मारा गया सोचे "मैं मारा गया" — दोनों ही नहीं समझते। यह आत्मा न तो मारता है, न मारा जाता है।
verses.commentary: A famous verse echoed in the Bhagavad Gītā (2.19). Both the killer's and the victim's identification are mistaken — both identify with the body. The Self in either is untouched.
verses.wordMeaning: A famous verse echoed in the Bhagavad Gītā (2.19). Both the killer's and the victim's identification are mistaken — both identify with the body. The Self in either is untouched.

verses.sanskrit: अणोरणीयान्महतो महीयानात्मास्य जन्तोर्निहितो गुहायाम् | तमक्रतुः पश्यति वीतशोको धातुप्रसादान्महिमानमात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: aṇoraṇīyānmahato mahīyānātmāsya jantornihito guhāyām | tamakratuḥ paśyati vītaśoko dhātuprasādānmahimānamātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: Smaller than the smallest, greater than the greatest — the Self is set in the heart of every creature. The desireless one, free of sorrow, by the grace of the Maker, sees the majesty of the Self.
verses.hindi: अणु से अणु, महान् से महान् — यह आत्मा प्राणी के हृदय-गुहा में स्थित है। निष्काम, शोक-रहित पुरुष — धातु (सृष्टा) की कृपा से आत्मा की महिमा को देखता है।
verses.commentary: The Self simultaneously pervades all (greater than the greatest) yet is present in every point (smaller than the smallest). It is in the heart-cave of every creature. Vision requires absence of desire and sorrow plus grace.
verses.wordMeaning: The Self simultaneously pervades all (greater than the greatest) yet is present in every point (smaller than the smallest). It is in the heart-cave of every creature. Vision requires absence of desire and sorrow plus grace.

verses.sanskrit: आसीनो दूरं व्रजति शयानो याति सर्वतः | कस्तं मदामदं देवं मदन्यो ज्ञातुमर्हति ||
verses.transliteration: āsīno dūraṃ vrajati śayāno yāti sarvataḥ | kastaṃ madāmadaṃ devaṃ madanyo jñātumarhati ||
verses.translation: Sitting, he travels far; lying, he goes everywhere. Who but I can know that joyful-and-not-joyful god?
verses.hindi: बैठा हुआ वह दूर जाता है; लेटा हुआ वह सब ओर पहुँचता है। उस मद-अमद (आनन्द-रूप परन्तु मद-रहित) देव को मेरे (मृत्यु के) अतिरिक्त कौन जान सकता है?
verses.commentary: The paradox of the Self's locomotion: still, yet covering all distances; recumbent, yet pervading. Yama claims privileged knowledge — knowable to him among the few.
verses.wordMeaning: The paradox of the Self's locomotion: still, yet covering all distances; recumbent, yet pervading. Yama claims privileged knowledge — knowable to him among the few.

verses.sanskrit: अशरीरं शरीरेष्वनवस्थेष्ववस्थितम् | महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ||
verses.transliteration: aśarīraṃ śarīreṣvanavastheṣvavasthitam | mahāntaṃ vibhumātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati ||
verses.translation: Bodiless among bodies; stable among the unstable; great, all-pervading — knowing the Self thus, the wise one does not grieve.
verses.hindi: अशरीर — परन्तु शरीरों में निवास करने वाला; अनवस्थ (नश्वर) के बीच स्थित (नित्य); महान्, विभु — ऐसे आत्मा को जानकर धीर पुरुष शोक नहीं करता।
verses.commentary: Three contrasts: bodiless within bodies, stable within instabilities, vast within smallness. To know the Self with these contrasts seen clearly is to leave grief.
verses.wordMeaning: Three contrasts: bodiless within bodies, stable within instabilities, vast within smallness. To know the Self with these contrasts seen clearly is to leave grief.

verses.sanskrit: नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन | यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यस्तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूं स्वाम् ||
verses.transliteration: nāyamātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena | yamevaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyastasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām ||
verses.translation: This Self is not attained by discourse, nor by intellect, nor by much hearing. Whom the Self itself chooses — by him alone is it attained; to him this Self reveals its own form.
verses.hindi: यह आत्मा न प्रवचन से, न मेधा से, न बहुश्रुति से प्राप्त होता है। जिसको यह स्वयं वरण कर लेता है — उसी को प्राप्त होता है; उसी के सामने यह आत्मा अपना तनु (रूप) प्रकट करता है।
verses.commentary: The grace dimension. Study and intellect prepare the ground but cannot deliver the recognition. The Self chooses the one in whom it will reveal itself. This is given, not earned.
verses.wordMeaning: The grace dimension. Study and intellect prepare the ground but cannot deliver the recognition. The Self chooses the one in whom it will reveal itself. This is given, not earned.

verses.sanskrit: नाविरतो दुश्चरितान्नाशान्तो नासमाहितः | नाशान्तमानसो वापि प्रज्ञानेनैनमाप्नुयात् ||
verses.transliteration: nāvirato duścaritānnāśānto nāsamāhitaḥ | nāśāntamānaso vāpi prajñānenainamāpnuyāt ||
verses.translation: Not he who has not desisted from wrong conduct, not he who is restless, not he whose mind is not collected — even by knowledge — none of these can attain this Self.
verses.hindi: जो दुश्चरित से विरत नहीं, जो शान्त नहीं, जो समाहित नहीं, जिसका मानस अशान्त है — ऐसा कोई भी, प्रज्ञान के द्वारा भी, इसे प्राप्त नहीं कर सकता।
verses.commentary: The exclusion list. Bad conduct, restlessness, scattered attention, agitated mind — any one of these disqualifies. The qualifications are ethical and attentional, not intellectual.
verses.wordMeaning: The exclusion list. Bad conduct, restlessness, scattered attention, agitated mind — any one of these disqualifies. The qualifications are ethical and attentional, not intellectual.

verses.sanskrit: यस्य ब्रह्म च क्षत्रं च उभे भवत ओदनः | मृत्युर्यस्योपसेचनं क इत्था वेद यत्र सः ||
verses.transliteration: yasya brahma ca kṣatraṃ ca ubhe bhavata odanaḥ | mṛtyuryasyopasecanaṃ ka itthā veda yatra saḥ ||
verses.translation: He whose food is both brāhmaṇa and kṣatriya, and whose seasoning is death — who indeed knows where he is?
verses.hindi: जिसका भोजन ब्राह्मण और क्षत्रिय दोनों हैं, और जिसका उपसेचन (व्यञ्जन) मृत्यु है — वह कहाँ है, यह कौन जानता है?
verses.commentary: A startling closing image. Brahman 'eats' even the highest and lowest social categories; death is just the seasoning. Who can locate such a being? The verse asserts the radical incomprehensibility of the Self to ordinary categories.
verses.wordMeaning: A startling closing image. Brahman 'eats' even the highest and lowest social categories; death is just the seasoning. Who can locate such a being? The verse asserts the radical incomprehensibility of the Self to ordinary categories.

verses.sanskrit: ऋतं पिबन्तौ सुकृतस्य लोके गुहां प्रविष्टौ परमे परार्धे | छायातपौ ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति पञ्चाग्नयो ये च त्रिणाचिकेताः ||
verses.transliteration: ṛtaṃ pibantau sukṛtasya loke guhāṃ praviṣṭau parame parārdhe | chāyātapau brahmavido vadanti pañcāgnayo ye ca triṇāciketāḥ ||
verses.translation: Two drink of ṛta in the world of good works — entered the cave, in the supreme half. Shadow and sunlight, knowers of Brahman call them — the five-fire performers and the thrice-Nāciketas practitioners.
verses.hindi: दो — पुण्य-लोक में ऋत (कर्म-फल) पीते हुए, गुहा (हृदय) में प्रविष्ट, परम पराध में स्थित — छाया-आतप के समान, उन्हें ब्रह्म-वेत्ता तथा पञ्चाग्नि-विद् और त्रिणाचिकेत-यजी कहते हैं।
verses.commentary: Two principles inhabit the cave: the individual self and the supreme Self. They are like shadow and sunlight — different in nature but inseparable in scene. Knowers and ritualists alike recognize the pair.
verses.wordMeaning: Two principles inhabit the cave: the individual self and the supreme Self. They are like shadow and sunlight — different in nature but inseparable in scene. Knowers and ritualists alike recognize the pair.

verses.sanskrit: यः सेतुरीजानानामक्षरं ब्रह्म यत्परम् | अभयं तितीर्षतां पारं नाचिकेतं शकेमहि ||
verses.transliteration: yaḥ seturījānānāmakṣaraṃ brahma yatparam | abhayaṃ titīrṣatāṃ pāraṃ nāciketaṃ śakemahi ||
verses.translation: May we be able (to perform) the Nāciketa fire — the bridge for those who sacrifice, the imperishable supreme Brahman, the fearless further shore for those who seek to cross.
verses.hindi: जो यज्ञ करने वालों का सेतु है, जो अक्षर परम ब्रह्म है, जो पार जाने वालों के लिये अभय का परम-पार है — उस नाचिकेत-अग्नि को हम सिद्ध कर सकें।
verses.commentary: Prayer for the capacity to perform the Nāciketa rite — described as the bridge, the imperishable, the fearless shore. One rite carries three superlatives.
verses.wordMeaning: Prayer for the capacity to perform the Nāciketa rite — described as the bridge, the imperishable, the fearless shore. One rite carries three superlatives.

verses.sanskrit: आत्मानं रथिनं विद्धि शरीरं रथमेव तु | बुद्धिं तु सारथिं विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहमेव च ||
verses.transliteration: ātmānaṃ rathinaṃ viddhi śarīraṃ rathameva tu | buddhiṃ tu sārathiṃ viddhi manaḥ pragrahameva ca ||
verses.translation: Know the Self as the rider, the body as the chariot. Know the intellect as the charioteer, and the mind as the reins.
verses.hindi: आत्मा को रथी जान, शरीर को रथ। बुद्धि को सारथी जान, मन को लगाम।
verses.commentary: The most celebrated metaphor of Indian philosophy. Self = passenger (pure witness). Body = vehicle. Intellect (buddhi) = driver. Mind = reins.
verses.wordMeaning: The most celebrated metaphor of Indian philosophy. Self = passenger (pure witness). Body = vehicle. Intellect (buddhi) = driver. Mind = reins.

verses.sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि हयानाहुर्विषयांस्तेषु गोचरान् | आत्मेन्द्रियमनोयुक्तं भोक्तेत्याहुर्मनीषिणः ||
verses.transliteration: indriyāṇi hayānāhurviṣayāṃsteṣu gocarān | ātmendriyamanoyuktaṃ bhoktetyāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ ||
verses.translation: The senses are the horses; sense-objects are their pastures. The wise call the Self — joined with body, senses, and mind — the enjoyer.
verses.hindi: इन्द्रियों को घोड़े और विषयों को उनका चरागाह कहा जाता है। शरीर-इन्द्रिय-मन से युक्त आत्मा को विद्वान् "भोक्ता" कहते हैं।
verses.commentary: The senses, like horses, naturally pull toward their objects. Without a skilled charioteer, they drag the rider into pleasure, distraction, addiction. The 'enjoyer' is the whole vehicle in motion.
verses.wordMeaning: The senses, like horses, naturally pull toward their objects. Without a skilled charioteer, they drag the rider into pleasure, distraction, addiction. The 'enjoyer' is the whole vehicle in motion.

verses.sanskrit: यस्त्वविज्ञानवान् भवत्ययुक्तेन मनसा सदा | तस्येन्द्रियाण्यवश्यानि दुष्टाश्वा इव सारथेः ||
verses.transliteration: yastvavijñānavān bhavatyayuktena manasā sadā | tasyendriyāṇyavaśyāni duṣṭāśvā iva sāratheḥ ||
verses.translation: He who has no understanding, whose mind is unyoked — his senses are uncontrollable, like wild horses for a charioteer.
verses.hindi: जो अज्ञानी है, जिसका मन अयुक्त (अव्यवस्थित) है — उसकी इन्द्रियाँ वश में नहीं रहतीं — जैसे सारथी के लिये दुष्ट अश्व।
verses.commentary: Without buddhi and yoked manas, the senses run wild. The charioteer's failure means the horses bolt. The whole chariot is endangered.
verses.wordMeaning: Without buddhi and yoked manas, the senses run wild. The charioteer's failure means the horses bolt. The whole chariot is endangered.

verses.sanskrit: यस्तु विज्ञानवान् भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा | तस्येन्द्रियाणि वश्यानि सदश्वा इव सारथेः ||
verses.transliteration: yastu vijñānavān bhavati yuktena manasā sadā | tasyendriyāṇi vaśyāni sadaśvā iva sāratheḥ ||
verses.translation: But he who has understanding, whose mind is always yoked — his senses are under control, like good horses for a charioteer.
verses.hindi: परन्तु जो ज्ञानी है, जिसका मन सदा युक्त (नियन्त्रित) है — उसकी इन्द्रियाँ वश में रहती हैं — जैसे सारथी के लिये सद्-अश्व।
verses.commentary: The contrast. With buddhi-understanding and a yoked mind, senses become 'good horses' — willingly responsive. The vehicle reaches its goal.
verses.wordMeaning: The contrast. With buddhi-understanding and a yoked mind, senses become 'good horses' — willingly responsive. The vehicle reaches its goal.

verses.sanskrit: यस्त्वविज्ञानवान् भवत्यमनस्कः सदाशुचिः | न स तत्पदमाप्नोति संसारं चाधिगच्छति ||
verses.transliteration: yastvavijñānavān bhavatyamanaskaḥ sadāśuciḥ | na sa tatpadamāpnoti saṃsāraṃ cādhigacchati ||
verses.translation: He who has no understanding, who is mindless and ever impure — does not attain that abode; he goes round and round in saṃsāra.
verses.hindi: जो अज्ञानी, मन-रहित, सदा अशुचि है — वह उस परम पद को नहीं प्राप्त करता; वह संसार में ही घूमता रहता है।
verses.commentary: The fate of the unguided life: no destination reached; the same circuit repeated. Saṃsāra is not 'rebirth' alone — it is the same patterns endlessly repeating.
verses.wordMeaning: The fate of the unguided life: no destination reached; the same circuit repeated. Saṃsāra is not 'rebirth' alone — it is the same patterns endlessly repeating.

verses.sanskrit: यस्तु विज्ञानवान् भवति समनस्कः सदा शुचिः | स तु तत्पदमाप्नोति यस्माद्भूयो न जायते ||
verses.transliteration: yastu vijñānavān bhavati samanaskaḥ sadā śuciḥ | sa tu tatpadamāpnoti yasmādbhūyo na jāyate ||
verses.translation: But he who has understanding, whose mind is collected, who is ever pure — attains that abode from which he is not born again.
verses.hindi: परन्तु जो ज्ञानी है, समाहित-मन वाला है, सदा शुचि है — वह उस परम पद को प्राप्त करता है, जहाँ से फिर जन्म नहीं होता।
verses.commentary: The mirror verse. Understanding + collected mind + purity = attainment of the abode of no-return. Three conditions, one outcome.
verses.wordMeaning: The mirror verse. Understanding + collected mind + purity = attainment of the abode of no-return. Three conditions, one outcome.

verses.sanskrit: विज्ञानसारथिर्यस्तु मनःप्रग्रहवान्नरः | सोऽध्वनः पारमाप्नोति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ||
verses.transliteration: vijñānasārathiryastu manaḥpragrahavānnaraḥ | so'dhvanaḥ pāramāpnoti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ||
verses.translation: The man who has understanding as his charioteer, who holds the reins of the mind — he reaches the end of the road, the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
verses.hindi: जिसका सारथी विज्ञान है, और जो मन की लगाम धारण करता है — वह मार्ग के पार पहुँचता है — विष्णु का परम पद।
verses.commentary: The chariot reaches its destination: the supreme abode of Viṣṇu. The verse names the goal. Viṣṇu here is the all-pervading principle — not denominationally restricted.
verses.wordMeaning: The chariot reaches its destination: the supreme abode of Viṣṇu. The verse names the goal. Viṣṇu here is the all-pervading principle — not denominationally restricted.

verses.sanskrit: इन्द्रियेभ्यः परा ह्यर्था अर्थेभ्यश्च परं मनः | मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्बुद्धेरात्मा महान् परः ||
verses.transliteration: indriyebhyaḥ parā hyarthā arthebhyaśca paraṃ manaḥ | manasastu parā buddhirbuddherātmā mahān paraḥ ||
verses.translation: Higher than the senses are the sense-objects; higher than the objects is the mind; higher than the mind is the intellect; higher than the intellect is the Great Self.
verses.hindi: इन्द्रियों से अर्थ (विषय) श्रेष्ठ; अर्थों से मन श्रेष्ठ; मन से बुद्धि श्रेष्ठ; बुद्धि से महान् आत्मा श्रेष्ठ।
verses.commentary: Hierarchy of subtlety. Each level subtler and more fundamental than the last. Practice that addresses only the senses cannot reach what is far subtler.
verses.wordMeaning: Hierarchy of subtlety. Each level subtler and more fundamental than the last. Practice that addresses only the senses cannot reach what is far subtler.

verses.sanskrit: महतः परमव्यक्तमव्यक्तात्पुरुषः परः | पुरुषान्न परं किञ्चित्सा काष्ठा सा परा गतिः ||
verses.transliteration: mahataḥ paramavyaktamavyaktātpuruṣaḥ paraḥ | puruṣānna paraṃ kiñcitsā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ ||
verses.translation: Higher than the Great is the Unmanifest; higher than the Unmanifest is the Person. There is nothing higher than the Person — that is the limit, that is the highest goal.
verses.hindi: महान् से अव्यक्त श्रेष्ठ; अव्यक्त से पुरुष श्रेष्ठ। पुरुष से ऊँचा कुछ नहीं — वही सीमा है, वही परम गति।
verses.commentary: The hierarchy continues: above the Great Self is the Unmanifest (avyakta — primordial undifferentiated state); above that, the Puruṣa. Beyond the Puruṣa, nothing. The terminus is reached.
verses.wordMeaning: The hierarchy continues: above the Great Self is the Unmanifest (avyakta — primordial undifferentiated state); above that, the Puruṣa. Beyond the Puruṣa, nothing. The terminus is reached.

verses.sanskrit: एष सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढोऽऽत्मा न प्रकाशते | दृश्यते त्वग्र्यया बुद्ध्या सूक्ष्मया सूक्ष्मदर्शिभिः ||
verses.transliteration: eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍho''tmā na prakāśate | dṛśyate tvagryayā buddhyā sūkṣmayā sūkṣmadarśibhiḥ ||
verses.translation: This Self is hidden in all beings — it does not shine forth. But it is seen by the keen, subtle intellect of those who see the subtle.
verses.hindi: यह आत्मा सब प्राणियों में गूढ़ है — प्रकट नहीं होता। परन्तु अग्र्या (तीक्ष्ण) सूक्ष्म बुद्धि वाले सूक्ष्म-दर्शी इसे देखते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Self is universal but hidden. Vision requires a sharpened buddhi — agryā, sūkṣmā. The same faculty that ordinarily looks outward must be redirected inward.
verses.wordMeaning: The Self is universal but hidden. Vision requires a sharpened buddhi — agryā, sūkṣmā. The same faculty that ordinarily looks outward must be redirected inward.

verses.sanskrit: यच्छेद्वाङ्मनसी प्राज्ञस्तद्यच्छेज्ज्ञान आत्मनि | ज्ञानमात्मनि महति नियच्छेत्तद्यच्छेच्छान्त आत्मनि ||
verses.transliteration: yacchedvāṅmanasī prājñastadyacchejjñāna ātmani | jñānamātmani mahati niyacchettadyacchecchānta ātmani ||
verses.translation: The wise should restrain speech in mind; restrain that in the knowing-self; restrain knowledge in the Great Self; restrain that in the peaceful Self.
verses.hindi: प्रज्ञ-पुरुष वाणी को मन में लय करे; मन को ज्ञान (बुद्धि) में लय करे; ज्ञान को महान् आत्मा में लय करे; उसे शान्त आत्मा में लय करे।
verses.commentary: The yoga of involution. Each level is dissolved into the next-higher: speech → mind → intellect → Great Self → peaceful Self. Outward speech contracts inward step by step.
verses.wordMeaning: The yoga of involution. Each level is dissolved into the next-higher: speech → mind → intellect → Great Self → peaceful Self. Outward speech contracts inward step by step.

verses.sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठत जाग्रत प्राप्य वरान्निबोधत | क्षुरस्य धारा निशिता दुरत्यया दुर्गं पथस्तत्कवयो वदन्ति ||
verses.transliteration: uttiṣṭhata jāgrata prāpya varānnibodhata | kṣurasya dhārā niśitā duratyayā durgaṃ pathastatkavayo vadanti ||
verses.translation: Arise! Awake! Having reached the wise ones, learn! The sharpened edge of a razor — hard to cross — difficult is the path, say the wise.
verses.hindi: उठो! जागो! श्रेष्ठ गुरुओं को प्राप्त करके सीखो! "तीक्ष्ण किये गये उस्तरे की धार के समान दुरत्यय" — दुर्गम है मार्ग — ऐसा ज्ञानी कहते हैं।
verses.commentary: The most famous call-to-action in the Upaniṣads: 'uttiṣṭhata jāgrata' — 'rise, awake!' Approach wise teachers; learn. The path is razor-edged. The verse galvanized Swami Vivekananda's life-mission.
verses.wordMeaning: The most famous call-to-action in the Upaniṣads: 'uttiṣṭhata jāgrata' — 'rise, awake!' Approach wise teachers; learn. The path is razor-edged. The verse galvanized Swami Vivekananda's life-mission.

verses.sanskrit: अशब्दमस्पर्शमरूपमव्ययं तथारसं नित्यमगन्धवच्च यत् | अनाद्यनन्तं महतः परं ध्रुवं निचाय्य तन्मृत्युमुखात् प्रमुच्यते ||
verses.transliteration: aśabdamasparśamarūpamavyayaṃ tathārasaṃ nityamagandhavacca yat | anādyanantaṃ mahataḥ paraṃ dhruvaṃ nicāyya tanmṛtyumukhāt pramucyate ||
verses.translation: Soundless, touchless, formless, undecaying, tasteless, eternal, scentless; without beginning or end, higher than the Great, fixed — knowing this, one is released from the mouth of Death.
verses.hindi: जो अशब्द, अस्पर्श, अरूप, अव्यय, अरस, नित्य, अगन्ध है; अनादि, अनन्त, महान् से परे, ध्रुव — उसको जानकर मनुष्य मृत्यु के मुख से छूट जाता है।
verses.commentary: Eight negations and three affirmations describing the Self. Knowing this releases from death's mouth. Yama himself, ironically, teaches how to be free of his domain.
verses.wordMeaning: Eight negations and three affirmations describing the Self. Knowing this releases from death's mouth. Yama himself, ironically, teaches how to be free of his domain.

verses.sanskrit: नाचिकेतमुपाख्यानं मृत्युप्रोक्तं सनातनम् | उक्त्वा श्रुत्वा च मेधावी ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ||
verses.transliteration: nāciketamupākhyānaṃ mṛtyuproktaṃ sanātanam | uktvā śrutvā ca medhāvī brahmaloke mahīyate ||
verses.translation: The eternal Nāciketa story, spoken by Death — speaking or hearing it, the wise one is exalted in the world of Brahman.
verses.hindi: मृत्यु-कथित यह नाचिकेत-उपाख्यान सनातन है — इसे कहने और सुनने वाला मेधावी ब्रह्म-लोक में महिमा को प्राप्त होता है।
verses.commentary: The text declares its own efficacy. Both reciter and listener gain access to the Brahma-world. Transmission itself is meritorious.
verses.wordMeaning: The text declares its own efficacy. Both reciter and listener gain access to the Brahma-world. Transmission itself is meritorious.

verses.sanskrit: य इमं परमं गुह्यं श्रावयेद्ब्रह्मसंसदि | प्रयतः श्राद्धकाले वा तदानन्त्याय कल्पते तदानन्त्याय कल्पत इति ||
verses.transliteration: ya imaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ śrāvayedbrahmasaṃsadi | prayataḥ śrāddhakāle vā tadānantyāya kalpate tadānantyāya kalpata iti ||
verses.translation: He who recites this supreme secret in an assembly of brahmins, or at the time of śrāddha, with reverence — it leads to infinity, it leads to infinity!
verses.hindi: जो इस परम गुह्य को ब्रह्म-सभा में अथवा श्राद्ध-काल में, प्रयत होकर सुनाता है — वह अनन्तता को प्राप्त करता है, अनन्तता को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: Closing of Vallī 3 with the doubled phrase — the marker of completion of a major section. The teaching, in proper context, leads to infinity.
verses.wordMeaning: Closing of Vallī 3 with the doubled phrase — the marker of completion of a major section. The teaching, in proper context, leads to infinity.

verses.sanskrit: पराञ्चि खानि व्यतृणत् स्वयम्भूस्तस्मात्पराङ् पश्यति नान्तरात्मन् | कश्चिद्धीरः प्रत्यगात्मानमैक्षदावृत्तचक्षुरमृतत्वमिच्छन् ||
verses.transliteration: parāñci khāni vyatṛṇat svayambhūstasmātparāṅ paśyati nāntarātman | kaścid dhīraḥ pratyagātmānamaikṣadāvṛttacakṣuramṛtatvamicchan ||
verses.translation: The Self-born pierced the openings outward — therefore one looks outward, not inward at the Self. Some wise one, desiring immortality, looked inward with reversed eyes and saw the inner Self.
verses.hindi: स्वयम्भू ने इन्द्रिय-छिद्रों को बहिर्मुख बनाया — इसीलिये मनुष्य बाहर देखता है, अन्तरात्मा को नहीं। कोई विरला धीर — अमरत्व की इच्छा से — आँखों को उल्टा करके अन्तरात्मा का दर्शन करता है।
verses.commentary: A pivotal verse on the direction of attention. The senses naturally face outward. To find the Self, the seeker must reverse the gaze — 'āvṛtta-cakṣuḥ.' Rare is the one who does it.
verses.wordMeaning: A pivotal verse on the direction of attention. The senses naturally face outward. To find the Self, the seeker must reverse the gaze — 'āvṛtta-cakṣuḥ.' Rare is the one who does it.

verses.sanskrit: पराचः कामाननुयन्ति बालास्ते मृत्योर्यन्ति विततस्य पाशम् | अथ धीरा अमृतत्वं विदित्वा ध्रुवमध्रुवेष्विह न प्रार्थयन्ते ||
verses.transliteration: parācaḥ kāmānanuyanti bālāste mṛtyoryanti vitatasya pāśam | atha dhīrā amṛtatvaṃ viditvā dhruvamadhruveṣviha na prārthayante ||
verses.translation: Children pursue outward desires; they walk into the spread-out noose of Death. But the wise, knowing immortality, do not seek the fixed among the unfixed here.
verses.hindi: बाल-बुद्धि लोग बहिर्मुख कामनाओं का अनुसरण करते हैं — वे मृत्यु के विस्तृत पाश में जा फँसते हैं। परन्तु धीर पुरुष — अमरत्व को जानकर — यहाँ के अध्रुव (नश्वर) पदार्थों में ध्रुव (नित्य) की खोज नहीं करते।
verses.commentary: Two strategies. Children chase the outward; the wise stop seeking permanence in the impermanent. The change is structural: they stop the category-mistake of expecting eternity from things-in-time.
verses.wordMeaning: Two strategies. Children chase the outward; the wise stop seeking permanence in the impermanent. The change is structural: they stop the category-mistake of expecting eternity from things-in-time.

verses.sanskrit: येन रूपं रसं गन्धं शब्दान् स्पर्शांश्च मैथुनान् | एतेनैव विजानाति किमत्र परिशिष्यते | एतद्वै तत् ||
verses.transliteration: yena rūpaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ śabdān sparśāṃśca maithunān | etenaiva vijānāti kimatra pariśiṣyate | etadvai tat ||
verses.translation: That by which one knows form, taste, smell, sounds, touch, and the pleasures of union — by that very thing all is known. What is left over here? This indeed is That.
verses.hindi: जिसके द्वारा रूप, रस, गन्ध, शब्द, स्पर्श, और मैथुन के सुख जाने जाते हैं — उसी से सब कुछ जाना जाता है। यहाँ और क्या शेष रहा? यही वह (आत्मा) है।
verses.commentary: The 'etad vai tat' phrase — 'this indeed is That' — will repeat through the rest of the Upaniṣad. The argument: behind every act of knowing is a single Knower. By that, all is known.
verses.wordMeaning: The 'etad vai tat' phrase — 'this indeed is That' — will repeat through the rest of the Upaniṣad. The argument: behind every act of knowing is a single Knower. By that, all is known.

verses.sanskrit: स्वप्नान्तं जागरितान्तं चोभौ येनानुपश्यति | महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ||
verses.transliteration: svapnāntaṃ jāgaritāntaṃ cobhau yenānupaśyati | mahāntaṃ vibhumātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati ||
verses.translation: That by which one sees both the dream-state and the waking-state — knowing it as the great, all-pervading Self, the wise one does not grieve.
verses.hindi: जिसके द्वारा स्वप्न-अन्त और जागृत-अन्त — दोनों देखे जाते हैं — उस महान् विभु आत्मा को जानकर धीर पुरुष शोक नहीं करता।
verses.commentary: The witness common to both waking and dream. That continuity across states reveals an awareness that is not bound to any one state. Knowing it ends grief.
verses.wordMeaning: The witness common to both waking and dream. That continuity across states reveals an awareness that is not bound to any one state. Knowing it ends grief.

verses.sanskrit: य इमं मध्वदं वेद आत्मानं जीवमन्तिकात् | ईशानं भूतभव्यस्य न ततो विजुगुप्सते | एतद्वै तत् ||
verses.transliteration: ya imaṃ madhvadaṃ veda ātmānaṃ jīvamantikāt | īśānaṃ bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate | etadvai tat ||
verses.translation: He who knows this honey-eater Self, the living, near at hand — the lord of past and future — from then on has no aversion. This indeed is That.
verses.hindi: जो इस मधु-भोक्ता आत्मा को — जीवित, निकट — भूत-भविष्य का स्वामी — जानता है — वह फिर किसी से घृणा नहीं करता। यही वह है।
verses.commentary: The Self is the 'eater of honey' — the experiencer of life's sweetness. To recognize it near at hand is to recognize the same Self in all beings — and aversion becomes impossible.
verses.wordMeaning: The Self is the 'eater of honey' — the experiencer of life's sweetness. To recognize it near at hand is to recognize the same Self in all beings — and aversion becomes impossible.

verses.sanskrit: यः पूर्वं तपसो जातमद्भ्यः पूर्वमजायत | गुहां प्रविश्य तिष्ठन्तं यो भूतेभिर्व्यपश्यत | एतद्वै तत् ||
verses.transliteration: yaḥ pūrvaṃ tapaso jātamadbhyaḥ pūrvamajāyata | guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantaṃ yo bhūtebhirvyapaśyata | etadvai tat ||
verses.translation: He who was born first from tapas, born before the waters, who, entering the cave, stands there — seen through the elements — this indeed is That.
verses.hindi: जो तप से पहले उत्पन्न हुआ, जो जल से भी पहले प्रकट हुआ, जो गुहा (हृदय) में प्रवेश करके वहाँ स्थित है, जो भूतों के द्वारा देखा जाता है — यही वह है।
verses.commentary: Cosmogonic identification. The Self pre-existed the elements; it dwells in the cave of the heart; it is what one sees through the play of phenomena. Origin and indweller are the same.
verses.wordMeaning: Cosmogonic identification. The Self pre-existed the elements; it dwells in the cave of the heart; it is what one sees through the play of phenomena. Origin and indweller are the same.

verses.sanskrit: या प्राणेन सम्भवत्यदितिर्देवतामयी | गुहां प्रविश्य तिष्ठन्तीं या भूतेभिर्व्यजायत | एतद्वै तत् ||
verses.transliteration: yā prāṇena sambhavatyaditirdevatāmayī | guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantīṃ yā bhūtebhirvyajāyata | etadvai tat ||
verses.translation: Aditi, made of the devas, who arises with the prāṇa, who entered the cave and stands there — who was born through the elements — this indeed is That.
verses.hindi: जो प्राण के साथ उत्पन्न होती है, जो देवता-मयी अदिति है, जो गुहा में प्रवेश करके स्थित है, जो भूतों के द्वारा प्रकट हुई — यही वह है।
verses.commentary: Aditi — the boundless mother — is identified with the Self. The cosmic-mother imagery deepens. She is born from prāṇa; she dwells in the cave; she manifests through the elements.
verses.wordMeaning: Aditi — the boundless mother — is identified with the Self. The cosmic-mother imagery deepens. She is born from prāṇa; she dwells in the cave; she manifests through the elements.

verses.sanskrit: अरण्योर्निहितो जातवेदा गर्भ इव सुभृतो गर्भिणीभिः | दिवे दिवे ईड्यो जागृवद्भिर्हविष्मद्भिर्मनुष्येभिरग्निः | एतद्वै तत् ||
verses.transliteration: araṇyornihito jātavedā garbha iva subhṛto garbhiṇībhiḥ | dive dive īḍyo jāgṛvadbhirhaviṣmadbhirmanuṣyebhiragniḥ | etadvai tat ||
verses.translation: Jātaveda (fire), set in two fire-sticks, well-nourished as an embryo by mothers — day by day to be praised by the watchful, offering-bearing men. This indeed is That.
verses.hindi: दो अरणियों में निहित जातवेद (अग्नि) — जैसे गर्भिणी के द्वारा गर्भ — दिन-दिन जागरूक, हविष्-धारी पुरुषों द्वारा पूज्य अग्नि — यही वह है।
verses.commentary: Fire as analogy. Latent in the two fire-sticks until friction releases it — like the Self latent in the body until practice releases it. Daily praise by alert practitioners.
verses.wordMeaning: Fire as analogy. Latent in the two fire-sticks until friction releases it — like the Self latent in the body until practice releases it. Daily praise by alert practitioners.

verses.sanskrit: यतश्चोदेति सूर्योऽस्तं यत्र च गच्छति | तं देवाः सर्वेऽर्पिताः तदु नात्येति कश्चन | एतद्वै तत् ||
verses.transliteration: yataścodeti sūryo'staṃ yatra ca gacchati | taṃ devāḥ sarve'rpitāḥ tadu nātyeti kaścana | etadvai tat ||
verses.translation: From which the sun rises and into which it sets — in that all the devas are placed. No one transcends it. This indeed is That.
verses.hindi: जिससे सूर्य उदय होता है और जिसमें अस्त होता है — उसी में सब देव स्थापित हैं। उसको कोई अतिक्रम नहीं करता। यही वह है।
verses.commentary: The Self is the substrate from which even the sun rises and into which it sets. All gods reside in it; none surpasses it. The cosmic ceiling.
verses.wordMeaning: The Self is the substrate from which even the sun rises and into which it sets. All gods reside in it; none surpasses it. The cosmic ceiling.

verses.sanskrit: यदेवेह तदमुत्र यदमुत्र तदन्विह | मृत्योः स मृत्युमाप्नोति य इह नानेव पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: yadeveha tadamutra yadamutra tadanviha | mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyumāpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati ||
verses.translation: What is here is there; what is there is here. He who sees many here goes from death to death.
verses.hindi: जो यहाँ है, वही वहाँ है; जो वहाँ है, वही यहाँ है। जो यहाँ बहुलता देखता है, वह मृत्यु से मृत्यु को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: A pillar verse. There is no 'here' and 'there'; one Self is both. To see many is to walk the wheel of death repeatedly. Non-dual seeing is the exit.
verses.wordMeaning: A pillar verse. There is no 'here' and 'there'; one Self is both. To see many is to walk the wheel of death repeatedly. Non-dual seeing is the exit.

verses.sanskrit: मनसैवेदमाप्तव्यं नेह नानास्ति किञ्चन | मृत्योः स मृत्युं गच्छति य इह नानेव पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: manasaivedamāptavyaṃ neha nānāsti kiñcana | mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyuṃ gacchati ya iha nāneva paśyati ||
verses.translation: By the mind alone this is to be attained: there is no diversity here whatsoever. He who sees diversity here goes from death to death.
verses.hindi: इसको मन से ही प्राप्त करना है — यहाँ कोई नाना (बहुलता) नहीं। जो यहाँ नाना देखता है, वह मृत्यु से मृत्यु को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The instruction is repeated for emphasis. The same warning, sharpened: by mind alone — not senses, not speech — is the unity attained. Diversity-perception is structurally fatal.
verses.wordMeaning: The instruction is repeated for emphasis. The same warning, sharpened: by mind alone — not senses, not speech — is the unity attained. Diversity-perception is structurally fatal.
