verses.sanskrit: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषो मध्य आत्मनि तिष्ठति | ईशानो भूतभव्यस्य न ततो विजुगुप्सते | एतद्वै तत् ||
verses.transliteration: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo madhya ātmani tiṣṭhati | īśāno bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate | etadvai tat ||
verses.translation: The Person of the size of a thumb dwells in the middle of the body — the lord of past and future. From him on there is no aversion. This indeed is That.
verses.hindi: अंगुष्ठ-मात्र पुरुष शरीर के मध्य में आत्मा में स्थित है — भूत-भविष्य का स्वामी। उसे जानकर मनुष्य फिर किसी से घृणा नहीं करता। यही वह है।
verses.commentary: The aṅguṣṭha-mātra image: the Self as a thumb-sized presence in the heart. Symbolic, not literal. The 'small' image makes the Self meditatively accessible.
verses.wordMeaning: The aṅguṣṭha-mātra image: the Self as a thumb-sized presence in the heart. Symbolic, not literal. The 'small' image makes the Self meditatively accessible.

verses.sanskrit: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषो ज्योतिरिवाधूमकः | ईशानो भूतभव्यस्य स एवाद्य स उ श्वः | एतद्वै तत् ||
verses.transliteration: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo jyotirivādhūmakaḥ | īśāno bhūtabhavyasya sa evādya sa u śvaḥ | etadvai tat ||
verses.translation: The thumb-sized Person is like a smokeless flame — lord of past and future. He alone is today; he alone tomorrow. This indeed is That.
verses.hindi: अंगुष्ठ-मात्र पुरुष — निर्धूम ज्योति जैसा — भूत-भविष्य का स्वामी। आज भी वही, कल भी वही। यही वह है।
verses.commentary: The 'smokeless flame' is one of the most beautiful images: pure light, no impurity, no consumption. He is today and tomorrow — the constant across all times.
verses.wordMeaning: The 'smokeless flame' is one of the most beautiful images: pure light, no impurity, no consumption. He is today and tomorrow — the constant across all times.

verses.sanskrit: यथोदकं दुर्गे वृष्टं पर्वतेषु विधावति | एवं धर्मान् पृथक् पश्यंस्तानेवानुविधावति ||
verses.transliteration: yathodakaṃ durge vṛṣṭaṃ parvateṣu vidhāvati | evaṃ dharmān pṛthak paśyaṃstānevānuvidhāvati ||
verses.translation: As rain fallen on a rugged mountain runs down its sides — even so, one who sees the dharmas (qualities) as separate runs after them.
verses.hindi: जैसे ऊबड़-खाबड़ पर्वत पर वर्षा का जल पहाड़ों पर बह जाता है — वैसे ही जो धर्मों को पृथक्-पृथक् देखता है, उन्हीं के पीछे दौड़ता है।
verses.commentary: An image of dispersion. Rain on a rugged mountain runs in many directions. Similarly, perception of separateness scatters one's attention and energy.
verses.wordMeaning: An image of dispersion. Rain on a rugged mountain runs in many directions. Similarly, perception of separateness scatters one's attention and energy.

verses.sanskrit: यथोदकं शुद्धे शुद्धमासिक्तं तादृगेव भवति | एवं मुनेर्विजानत आत्मा भवति गौतम ||
verses.transliteration: yathodakaṃ śuddhe śuddhamāsiktaṃ tādṛgeva bhavati | evaṃ munervijānata ātmā bhavati gautama ||
verses.translation: As pure water poured into pure water becomes simply the same — so the Self of the knowing sage, O Gautama (Naciketas), becomes (one with the Self).
verses.hindi: जैसे शुद्ध जल शुद्ध जल में डालने पर एक ही हो जाता है — वैसे ही, हे गौतम (नचिकेता)! ज्ञानी मुनि का आत्मा (परम आत्मा) हो जाता है।
verses.commentary: Closing image of the vallī: water-into-water. The knower's individual self merges into the universal Self without residue. There is no 'two waters' afterward.
verses.wordMeaning: Closing image of the vallī: water-into-water. The knower's individual self merges into the universal Self without residue. There is no 'two waters' afterward.

verses.sanskrit: पुरमेकादशद्वारमजस्यावक्रचेतसः | अनुष्ठाय न शोचति विमुक्तश्च विमुच्यते | एतद्वै तत् ||
verses.transliteration: puramekādaśadvāramajasyāvakracetasaḥ | anuṣṭhāya na śocati vimuktaśca vimucyate | etadvai tat ||
verses.translation: The city of eleven gates belongs to the unborn one of unwarped consciousness. Meditating on him, one does not grieve; freed, one is liberated. This indeed is That.
verses.hindi: अज (अजन्मा) — अकुटिल-चेतन — का यह एकादश-द्वारी (ग्यारह द्वारों वाला) नगर है। उसका अनुष्ठान करने से मनुष्य शोक नहीं करता; मुक्त होकर सर्वथा मुक्त हो जाता है। यही वह है।
verses.commentary: The body is a city with eleven gates (7 in head, 2 below, navel, and brahma-randhra). Its lord is the unborn Self. Meditating on him as the indweller frees one from grief and finally from all bondage.
verses.wordMeaning: The body is a city with eleven gates (7 in head, 2 below, navel, and brahma-randhra). Its lord is the unborn Self. Meditating on him as the indweller frees one from grief and finally from all bondage.

verses.sanskrit: हंसः शुचिषद्वसुरन्तरिक्षसद् होता वेदिषदतिथिर्दुरोणसत् | नृषद्वरसदृतसद्व्योमसदब्जा गोजा ऋतजा अद्रिजा ऋतं बृहत् ||
verses.transliteration: haṃsaḥ śuciṣadvasurantarikṣasad hotā vediṣadatithirduroṇasat | nṛṣadvarasadṛtasadvyomasadabjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtaṃ bṛhat ||
verses.translation: He is the swan in the pure (sky), the vasu in the middle space, the priest at the altar, the guest in the house; he dwells in men, in gods, in ṛta, in the void; born of water, born of cattle, born of ṛta, born of rock — Ṛta, the great.
verses.hindi: वही पवित्र आकाश में हंस है, अन्तरिक्ष में वसु, वेदी पर होता, द्रोणी (पात्र) में अतिथि; नृषद्, वरसद्, ऋतसद्, व्योमसद्; जल से उत्पन्न, गौ से उत्पन्न, ऋत से उत्पन्न, अद्रि से उत्पन्न — महान् ऋत वही है।
verses.commentary: A cascade of identifications. The Self is in every locus and every form. The Vedic vocabulary piles up: swan, priest, guest, all 'dwellers' in different spheres — and all are one.
verses.wordMeaning: A cascade of identifications. The Self is in every locus and every form. The Vedic vocabulary piles up: swan, priest, guest, all 'dwellers' in different spheres — and all are one.

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वं प्राणमुन्नयत्यपानं प्रत्यगस्यति | मध्ये वामनमासीनं विश्वे देवा उपासते ||
verses.transliteration: ūrdhvaṃ prāṇamunnayatyapānaṃ pratyagasyati | madhye vāmanamāsīnaṃ viśve devā upāsate ||
verses.translation: He leads the prāṇa upward, the apāna downward. The vāmana (the dwarf, the inner Self) sitting in the middle — all the gods worship him.
verses.hindi: वह प्राण को ऊपर ले जाता है, अपान को नीचे फेंकता है। मध्य में बैठे वामन (छोटे — सूक्ष्म आत्मा) की सब देव उपासना करते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Self regulates the breath without thought. Upward and downward streams meet in the middle — where the 'vāmana' (small one) sits. All inner powers center on this midpoint.
verses.wordMeaning: The Self regulates the breath without thought. Upward and downward streams meet in the middle — where the 'vāmana' (small one) sits. All inner powers center on this midpoint.

verses.sanskrit: अस्य विस्रंसमानस्य शरीरस्थस्य देहिनः | देहाद्विमुच्यमानस्य किमत्र परिशिष्यते | एतद्वै तत् ||
verses.transliteration: asya visraṃsamānasya śarīrasthasya dehinaḥ | dehādvimucyamānasya kimatra pariśiṣyate | etadvai tat ||
verses.translation: Of this body-dweller, when the body crumbles and the dweller is released — what remains here? This indeed is That.
verses.hindi: इस शरीर-स्थ देही के शरीर के क्षय होने पर — जब वह देह से छूट जाता है — तब यहाँ क्या शेष रहता है? यही वह है।
verses.commentary: A question with its own answer encoded. When body and indweller separate, what's left? Not the body — that decays. What remains is what was never in the body to begin with: the Self. 'Etad vai tat.'
verses.wordMeaning: A question with its own answer encoded. When body and indweller separate, what's left? Not the body — that decays. What remains is what was never in the body to begin with: the Self. 'Etad vai tat.'

verses.sanskrit: न प्राणेन नापानेन मर्त्यो जीवति कश्चन | इतरेण तु जीवन्ति यस्मिन्नेतावुपाश्रितौ ||
verses.transliteration: na prāṇena nāpānena martyo jīvati kaścana | itareṇa tu jīvanti yasminnetāvupāśritau ||
verses.translation: No mortal lives by prāṇa or apāna alone. They live by something else, in which these two are based.
verses.hindi: कोई भी मनुष्य केवल प्राण और अपान से जीवित नहीं रहता। वे किसी और के द्वारा जीवित हैं — जिसमें ये दोनों आश्रित हैं।
verses.commentary: Even breath is not life — breath rests on something deeper. The mechanical motion of inspiration and expiration is sustained by an animating presence. That is what lives.
verses.wordMeaning: Even breath is not life — breath rests on something deeper. The mechanical motion of inspiration and expiration is sustained by an animating presence. That is what lives.

verses.sanskrit: हन्त त इदं प्रवक्ष्यामि गुह्यं ब्रह्म सनातनम् | यथा च मरणं प्राप्य आत्मा भवति गौतम ||
verses.transliteration: hanta ta idaṃ pravakṣyāmi guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam | yathā ca maraṇaṃ prāpya ātmā bhavati gautama ||
verses.translation: Come now, I will tell you this secret, eternal Brahman — and how the Self fares upon reaching death, O Gautama.
verses.hindi: अब मैं तुझे यह गुह्य, सनातन ब्रह्म बताता हूँ — और बताता हूँ कि मृत्यु को प्राप्त करके आत्मा क्या होता है, हे गौतम!
verses.commentary: Yama returns to Naciketas's original question — the post-death fate of the Self. Now ready to answer fully, he announces.
verses.wordMeaning: Yama returns to Naciketas's original question — the post-death fate of the Self. Now ready to answer fully, he announces.

verses.sanskrit: योनिमन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते शरीरत्वाय देहिनः | स्थाणुमन्येऽनुसंयन्ति यथाकर्म यथाश्रुतम् ||
verses.transliteration: yonimanye prapadyante śarīratvāya dehinaḥ | sthāṇumanye'nusaṃyanti yathākarma yathāśrutam ||
verses.translation: Some embodied ones reach a womb for embodiment again; others enter into the stationary (plant or mineral) — according to their actions and their learning.
verses.hindi: कुछ देही फिर शरीर धारण करने के लिये योनि में जाते हैं; कुछ स्थावर (वृक्ष, पत्थर) में प्रवेश करते हैं — अपने कर्म और श्रुति के अनुसार।
verses.commentary: The doctrine of rebirth across kingdoms. Karma + śruti (learning) jointly determine the next vehicle. Embodiment is not random.
verses.wordMeaning: The doctrine of rebirth across kingdoms. Karma + śruti (learning) jointly determine the next vehicle. Embodiment is not random.

verses.sanskrit: य एष सुप्तेषु जागर्ति कामं कामं पुरुषो निर्मिमाणः | तदेव शुक्रं तद् ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते | तस्मिँल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन | एतद्वै तत् ||
verses.transliteration: ya eṣa supteṣu jāgarti kāmaṃ kāmaṃ puruṣo nirmimāṇaḥ | tadeva śukraṃ tad brahma tadevāmṛtamucyate | tasmiṃllokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tadu nātyeti kaścana | etadvai tat ||
verses.translation: The Person who is awake while others sleep, fashioning desire after desire — that is the bright, that is Brahman, that is called the immortal. In him all worlds are established; no one transcends him. This indeed is That.
verses.hindi: जो सोते हुओं के बीच भी जागता है — कामना-दर-कामना रचता हुआ — वही शुक्र (तेजोमय) है, वही ब्रह्म है, वही अमर कहा जाता है। उसी में सब लोक प्रतिष्ठित हैं; उसको कोई अतिक्रम नहीं करता। यही वह है।
verses.commentary: The Self is awake even in sleep — the dreamer behind the dreams. He fashions desires; in him all worlds rest. The verse asserts ultimate inwardness.
verses.wordMeaning: The Self is awake even in sleep — the dreamer behind the dreams. He fashions desires; in him all worlds rest. The verse asserts ultimate inwardness.

verses.sanskrit: अग्निर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव | एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च ||
verses.transliteration: agniryathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva | ekastathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiśca ||
verses.translation: As fire, one, having entered the world, takes a form corresponding to each form — so the One inner Self of all beings becomes a form corresponding to each form, and yet is outside it too.
verses.hindi: जैसे एक अग्नि — संसार में प्रवेश करके — प्रत्येक रूप के अनुरूप रूप धारण कर लेती है, वैसे ही एक अन्तरात्मा सब प्राणियों में रूप-रूप के अनुरूप होता है — और बाहर भी रहता है।
verses.commentary: The fire-and-many-forms image. The same fire takes the shape of every fuel it burns. So the one Self takes the apparent shape of every being it dwells in, while remaining itself beyond.
verses.wordMeaning: The fire-and-many-forms image. The same fire takes the shape of every fuel it burns. So the one Self takes the apparent shape of every being it dwells in, while remaining itself beyond.

verses.sanskrit: वायुर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव | एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च ||
verses.transliteration: vāyuryathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva | ekastathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiśca ||
verses.translation: As wind, one, having entered the world, takes a form corresponding to each form — so the One inner Self of all beings becomes a form corresponding to each form, and yet is outside it too.
verses.hindi: जैसे एक वायु संसार में प्रवेश करके प्रत्येक रूप के अनुरूप रूप धारण कर लेती है, वैसे ही एक अन्तरात्मा सब प्राणियों में रूप-रूप के अनुरूप होता है — और बाहर भी रहता है।
verses.commentary: Mirror verse with wind. Same teaching, different element. Repetition for emphasis: the truth holds across every substrate.
verses.wordMeaning: Mirror verse with wind. Same teaching, different element. Repetition for emphasis: the truth holds across every substrate.

verses.sanskrit: सूर्यो यथा सर्वलोकस्य चक्षुर्न लिप्यते चाक्षुषैर्बाह्यदोषैः | एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा न लिप्यते लोकदुःखेन बाह्यः ||
verses.transliteration: sūryo yathā sarvalokasya cakṣurna lipyate cākṣuṣairbāhyadoṣaiḥ | ekastathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā na lipyate lokaduḥkhena bāhyaḥ ||
verses.translation: As the sun, the eye of the whole world, is not tainted by external defects seen by the eye — so the One inner Self of all beings is not tainted by the sorrow of the world, being beyond it.
verses.hindi: जैसे सूर्य — सब लोकों का नेत्र — चाक्षुष बाह्य दोषों से लिप्त नहीं होता, वैसे ही सब प्राणियों का एक अन्तरात्मा — लोक-दुःख से लिप्त नहीं होता — वह बाह्य है।
verses.commentary: The sun illumines without being touched by what it illumines. So the Self illumines all experience — pleasant and painful — without being stained.
verses.wordMeaning: The sun illumines without being touched by what it illumines. So the Self illumines all experience — pleasant and painful — without being stained.

verses.sanskrit: एको वशी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा एकं रूपं बहुधा यः करोति | तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीरास्तेषां सुखं शाश्वतं नेतरेषाम् ||
verses.transliteration: eko vaśī sarvabhūtāntarātmā ekaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti | tamātmasthaṃ ye'nupaśyanti dhīrāsteṣāṃ sukhaṃ śāśvataṃ netareṣām ||
verses.translation: The one inner Self of all beings — the controller — makes one form into many. The wise who see him in the Self have eternal happiness; not the others.
verses.hindi: एक — सब प्राणियों का अन्तरात्मा — वशी (नियन्ता) — एक रूप को अनेक रूप में करता है। उसे आत्म-स्थ देखने वाले धीर पुरुषों को शाश्वत सुख होता है; अन्य को नहीं।
verses.commentary: Three claims in one verse. (1) The Self is one. (2) It is the controller. (3) Those who see it have eternal happiness — uniquely.
verses.wordMeaning: Three claims in one verse. (1) The Self is one. (2) It is the controller. (3) Those who see it have eternal happiness — uniquely.

verses.sanskrit: नित्योऽनित्यानां चेतनश्चेतनानामेको बहूनां यो विदधाति कामान् | तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीरास्तेषां शान्तिः शाश्वती नेतरेषाम् ||
verses.transliteration: nityo'nityānāṃ cetanaścetanānāmeko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān | tamātmasthaṃ ye'nupaśyanti dhīrāsteṣāṃ śāntiḥ śāśvatī netareṣām ||
verses.translation: The Eternal among the non-eternal; the Conscious among the conscious — the One who fulfills the desires of the many. The wise who see him in the Self have eternal peace; not the others.
verses.hindi: अनित्यों के बीच नित्य, चेतनों के बीच चेतन — जो एक होकर बहुतों की कामनाओं को पूर्ण करता है। उसे आत्म-स्थ देखने वाले धीर पुरुषों को शाश्वत शान्ति होती है; अन्य को नहीं।
verses.commentary: A famous formulation. The Eternal among the impermanent, the Conscious among the conscious — three superlative relations. Recognition produces peace.
verses.wordMeaning: A famous formulation. The Eternal among the impermanent, the Conscious among the conscious — three superlative relations. Recognition produces peace.

verses.sanskrit: तदेतदिति मन्यन्तेऽनिर्देश्यं परमं सुखम् | कथं नु तद्विजानीयां किमु भाति विभाति वा ||
verses.transliteration: tadetaditi manyante'nirdeśyaṃ paramaṃ sukham | kathaṃ nu tadvijānīyāṃ kimu bhāti vibhāti vā ||
verses.translation: (Naciketas asks:) They think of it as "this is that" — the indescribable supreme bliss. How shall I know it? Does it shine, or does it shine forth?
verses.hindi: वे "यही वह है" — ऐसा मानते हैं — अनिर्देश्य परम सुख। मैं उसे कैसे जानूँ? वह स्वयं चमकता है, या उसकी प्रभा से और कुछ चमकता है?
verses.commentary: The boy returns with the deepest question of perception. How does the supreme make itself known? Is it the shiner or is something shone-on?
verses.wordMeaning: The boy returns with the deepest question of perception. How does the supreme make itself known? Is it the shiner or is something shone-on?

verses.sanskrit: न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः | तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति ||
verses.transliteration: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto'yamagniḥ | tameva bhāntamanubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti ||
verses.translation: There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars; nor these lightnings — much less this fire. He shining, all shine after him; by his light all this is illumined.
verses.hindi: वहाँ न सूर्य चमकता है, न चन्द्र-तारे, न ये बिजली — फिर यह अग्नि कहाँ? वह चमकता है, और उसी के बाद सब चमकते हैं; उसी की प्रभा से यह सब प्रकाशित होता है।
verses.commentary: The same celebrated verse appears here as in Mundaka 2.2.11 (and Śvetāśvatara). Brahman is the light of lights — the precondition for any illumination at all. Naciketas's question is answered.
verses.wordMeaning: The same celebrated verse appears here as in Mundaka 2.2.11 (and Śvetāśvatara). Brahman is the light of lights — the precondition for any illumination at all. Naciketas's question is answered.

verses.sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वमूलोऽवाक्शाख एषोऽश्वत्थः सनातनः | तदेव शुक्रं तद् ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते | तस्मिँल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन | एतद्वै तत् ||
verses.transliteration: ūrdhvamūlo'vākśākha eṣo'śvatthaḥ sanātanaḥ | tadeva śukraṃ tad brahma tadevāmṛtamucyate | tasmiṃllokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tadu nātyeti kaścana | etadvai tat ||
verses.translation: Roots above, branches below — this is the eternal aśvattha tree. That is the bright; that is Brahman; that is called the immortal. In it all worlds are established; none transcends it. This indeed is That.
verses.hindi: ऊपर मूल और नीचे शाखाओं वाला यह सनातन अश्वत्थ है। वही शुक्र, वही ब्रह्म, वही अमर कहा जाता है। उसी में सब लोक प्रतिष्ठित हैं; उसको कोई अतिक्रम नहीं करता। यही वह है।
verses.commentary: The inverted-tree image — roots above (in Brahman), branches below (manifest world). Echoed in Bhagavad Gītā 15.1. The tree is sanātana (eternal); all worlds rest in it.
verses.wordMeaning: The inverted-tree image — roots above (in Brahman), branches below (manifest world). Echoed in Bhagavad Gītā 15.1. The tree is sanātana (eternal); all worlds rest in it.

verses.sanskrit: यदिदं किञ्च जगत् सर्वं प्राण एजति निःसृतम् | महद्भयं वज्रमुद्यतं य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ||
verses.transliteration: yadidaṃ kiñca jagat sarvaṃ prāṇa ejati niḥsṛtam | mahadbhayaṃ vajramudyataṃ ya etadviduramṛtāste bhavanti ||
verses.translation: All this universe, whatever exists, moves having come forth in the prāṇa (Brahman). It is a great terror, a raised thunderbolt. Those who know this become immortal.
verses.hindi: यह जो कुछ भी जगत् है — सब प्राण (ब्रह्म) से उत्पन्न होकर उसी में स्पन्दित होता है। वह महान् भय है, उठा हुआ वज्र है — जो इसे जानते हैं, वे अमर हो जाते हैं।
verses.commentary: Brahman as 'great terror' and 'raised thunderbolt' — the awe-inspiring sovereign in which all moves. Fear of Brahman is the wise fear; knowing it produces immortality.
verses.wordMeaning: Brahman as 'great terror' and 'raised thunderbolt' — the awe-inspiring sovereign in which all moves. Fear of Brahman is the wise fear; knowing it produces immortality.

verses.sanskrit: भयादस्याग्निस्तपति भयात्तपति सूर्यः | भयादिन्द्रश्च वायुश्च मृत्युर्धावति पञ्चमः ||
verses.transliteration: bhayādasyāgnistapati bhayāttapati sūryaḥ | bhayādindraśca vāyuśca mṛtyurdhāvati pañcamaḥ ||
verses.translation: Out of fear of him, fire burns; out of fear, the sun shines; out of fear, Indra, Vāyu, and Death — the fifth — runs.
verses.hindi: उसके भय से अग्नि तपता है, उसके भय से सूर्य चमकता है; उसके भय से इन्द्र और वायु, और पाँचवाँ मृत्यु — दौड़ता है।
verses.commentary: Cosmic discipline. Even fire, sun, Indra, wind, and Death himself perform their functions out of reverent compliance with the cosmic law. Order is maintained by awe.
verses.wordMeaning: Cosmic discipline. Even fire, sun, Indra, wind, and Death himself perform their functions out of reverent compliance with the cosmic law. Order is maintained by awe.

verses.sanskrit: इह चेदशकद्बोद्धुं प्राक्शरीरस्य विस्रसः | ततः सर्गेषु लोकेषु शरीरत्वाय कल्पते ||
verses.transliteration: iha cedaśakadboddhuṃ prākśarīrasya visrasaḥ | tataḥ sargeṣu lokeṣu śarīratvāya kalpate ||
verses.translation: If one is able to know him here, before the body falls away — well; otherwise one is fit for embodiment again in created worlds.
verses.hindi: यदि शरीर के गिरने से पहले ही यहाँ जान लिया जाये — तो ठीक; अन्यथा सर्ग-लोकों में पुनः शरीर के योग्य बना रहता है।
verses.commentary: The urgency. Self-realization is to be attempted in this very body, before death. Otherwise, the cycle of embodiment continues. The time is now.
verses.wordMeaning: The urgency. Self-realization is to be attempted in this very body, before death. Otherwise, the cycle of embodiment continues. The time is now.

verses.sanskrit: यथाऽऽदर्शे तथाऽऽत्मनि यथा स्वप्ने तथा पितृलोके | यथाप्सु परीव ददृशे तथा गन्धर्वलोके छायातपयोरिव ब्रह्मलोके ||
verses.transliteration: yathā''darśe tathā''tmani yathā svapne tathā pitṛloke | yathāpsu parīva dadṛśe tathā gandharvaloke chāyātapayoriva brahmaloke ||
verses.translation: As in a mirror, so in the Self; as in dream, so in the world of the ancestors; as if reflected in water, so in the world of the gandharvas; as light and shadow, so in the world of Brahman.
verses.hindi: जैसे दर्पण में, वैसे आत्मा में; जैसे स्वप्न में, वैसे पितृ-लोक में; जैसे जल में प्रतिबिम्ब, वैसे गन्धर्व-लोक में; जैसे छाया और प्रकाश, वैसे ब्रह्म-लोक में।
verses.commentary: Levels of clarity. The clearest perception (mirror) is the Self in self-knowledge. Dream-like perception in pitṛ-loka; water-reflection in gandharva-loka; light-and-shadow in brahma-loka. The hierarchy maps levels of subtle perception.
verses.wordMeaning: Levels of clarity. The clearest perception (mirror) is the Self in self-knowledge. Dream-like perception in pitṛ-loka; water-reflection in gandharva-loka; light-and-shadow in brahma-loka. The hierarchy maps levels of subtle perception.

verses.sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणां पृथग्भावमुदयास्तमयौ च यत् | पृथगुत्पद्यमानानां मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ||
verses.transliteration: indriyāṇāṃ pṛthagbhāvamudayāstamayau ca yat | pṛthagutpadyamānānāṃ matvā dhīro na śocati ||
verses.translation: Recognizing the distinct nature of the senses, their rising and setting separately — appearing distinctly — the wise one does not grieve.
verses.hindi: इन्द्रियों का पृथक्-पृथक् स्वरूप, उनका पृथक् रूप से उदय और अस्त, पृथक् उत्पत्ति — इसको जानकर धीर पुरुष शोक नहीं करता।
verses.commentary: Recognition of the senses as separate from the Self. They rise and set on their own; the Self does not rise and set. Holding this distinction clearly produces equanimity.
verses.wordMeaning: Recognition of the senses as separate from the Self. They rise and set on their own; the Self does not rise and set. Holding this distinction clearly produces equanimity.

verses.sanskrit: इन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनो मनसः सत्त्वमुत्तमम् | सत्त्वादधि महानात्मा महतोऽव्यक्तमुत्तमम् ||
verses.transliteration: indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ mano manasaḥ sattvamuttamam | sattvādadhi mahānātmā mahato'vyaktamuttamam ||
verses.translation: Higher than the senses is mind; higher than mind is sattva (intellect-substance); higher than sattva is the Great Self; higher than the Great is the Unmanifest.
verses.hindi: इन्द्रियों से मन श्रेष्ठ; मन से सत्त्व (बुद्धि) श्रेष्ठ; सत्त्व से महान् आत्मा; महान् से अव्यक्त श्रेष्ठ।
verses.commentary: Re-statement of the hierarchy (cf. 1.3.10–11). Each level subtler. Sustained inquiry climbs the hierarchy.
verses.wordMeaning: Re-statement of the hierarchy (cf. 1.3.10–11). Each level subtler. Sustained inquiry climbs the hierarchy.

verses.sanskrit: अव्यक्तात्तु परः पुरुषो व्यापकोऽलिङ्ग एव च | यं ज्ञात्वा मुच्यते जन्तुरमृतत्वं च गच्छति ||
verses.transliteration: avyaktāttu paraḥ puruṣo vyāpako'liṅga eva ca | yaṃ jñātvā mucyate janturamṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati ||
verses.translation: Higher than the Unmanifest is the Person — all-pervading and without distinguishing mark. Knowing him, a creature is freed and attains immortality.
verses.hindi: अव्यक्त से भी परम पुरुष — व्यापक, अलिङ्ग (कोई चिह्न नहीं) — जिसको जानकर प्राणी मुक्त होता है और अमरत्व प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The terminus of the climb: Puruṣa — all-pervading, marker-less, beyond every characterization. Knowing him: liberation and immortality.
verses.wordMeaning: The terminus of the climb: Puruṣa — all-pervading, marker-less, beyond every characterization. Knowing him: liberation and immortality.

verses.sanskrit: न संदृशे तिष्ठति रूपमस्य न चक्षुषा पश्यति कश्चनैनम् | हृदा मनीषा मनसाभिक्लृप्तो य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ||
verses.transliteration: na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpamasya na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaścanainam | hṛdā manīṣā manasābhikḷpto ya etadviduramṛtāste bhavanti ||
verses.translation: His form does not stand in the field of vision; no one sees him with the eye. By the heart, by deep insight, by the mind he is conceived. Those who know this become immortal.
verses.hindi: उसका रूप दृष्टि के सामने नहीं रहता; कोई उसे आँख से नहीं देखता। हृदय से, मनीषा से, मन से वह संकल्पित होता है। जो इसे जानते हैं, वे अमर हो जाते हैं।
verses.commentary: He cannot be seen by the eye; he is grasped by the heart, by insight, by mind. Three inner faculties take over where the outer eye fails.
verses.wordMeaning: He cannot be seen by the eye; he is grasped by the heart, by insight, by mind. Three inner faculties take over where the outer eye fails.

verses.sanskrit: यदा पञ्चावतिष्ठन्ते ज्ञानानि मनसा सह | बुद्धिश्च न विचेष्टते तामाहुः परमां गतिम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā pañcāvatiṣṭhante jñānāni manasā saha | buddhiśca na viceṣṭate tāmāhuḥ paramāṃ gatim ||
verses.translation: When the five faculties of knowledge together with the mind come to rest, and the intellect does not stir — that, they call the supreme state.
verses.hindi: जब पाँचों ज्ञानेन्द्रियाँ मन के साथ स्थिर हो जाती हैं, और बुद्धि भी विचलित नहीं होती — तब उसे परम गति कहा जाता है।
verses.commentary: Definition of samādhi. Five senses + mind + intellect — all six come to rest. That stillness is the supreme state.
verses.wordMeaning: Definition of samādhi. Five senses + mind + intellect — all six come to rest. That stillness is the supreme state.

verses.sanskrit: तां योगमिति मन्यन्ते स्थिरामिन्द्रियधारणाम् | अप्रमत्तस्तदा भवति योगो हि प्रभवाप्ययौ ||
verses.transliteration: tāṃ yogamiti manyante sthirāmindriyadhāraṇām | apramattastadā bhavati yogo hi prabhavāpyayau ||
verses.translation: That steady holding of the senses, they call yoga. One becomes alert then — for yoga is both origin and dissolution.
verses.hindi: इस स्थिर इन्द्रिय-धारणा को योग कहते हैं। तब मनुष्य अप्रमत्त (सजग) होता है — क्योंकि योग ही प्रभव और अप्यय है।
verses.commentary: First definition of yoga in Sanskrit literature: 'steady holding of the senses.' And a warning: yoga can arise and disappear. Alertness sustains it.
verses.wordMeaning: First definition of yoga in Sanskrit literature: 'steady holding of the senses.' And a warning: yoga can arise and disappear. Alertness sustains it.

verses.sanskrit: नैव वाचा न मनसा प्राप्तुं शक्यो न चक्षुषा | अस्तीति ब्रुवतोऽन्यत्र कथं तदुपलभ्यते ||
verses.transliteration: naiva vācā na manasā prāptuṃ śakyo na cakṣuṣā | astīti bruvato'nyatra kathaṃ tadupalabhyate ||
verses.translation: He cannot be reached by speech, mind, or eye. How can he be known otherwise than by one who says, 'He is'?
verses.hindi: वाणी से नहीं, न मन से, न नेत्र से वह प्राप्य है। "वह है" — यह कहने वाले के अतिरिक्त — और कैसे जाना जाये?
verses.commentary: A profound verse. The Self cannot be acquired through any faculty. But the conviction 'asti' — 'He is' — is itself the doorway. Faith in existence precedes knowledge of essence.
verses.wordMeaning: A profound verse. The Self cannot be acquired through any faculty. But the conviction 'asti' — 'He is' — is itself the doorway. Faith in existence precedes knowledge of essence.

verses.sanskrit: अस्तीत्येवोपलब्धव्यस्तत्त्वभावेन चोभयोः | अस्तीत्येवोपलब्धस्य तत्त्वभावः प्रसीदति ||
verses.transliteration: astītyevopalabdhavyastattvabhāvena cobhayoḥ | astītyevopalabdhasya tattvabhāvaḥ prasīdati ||
verses.translation: He is to be known as 'He is' — and then, by both (existence and essence). To one who has known 'He is,' the essential nature becomes clear.
verses.hindi: "वह है" — ऐसा ही जाना जाना चाहिये — और फिर तत्त्व-भाव से भी। जिसने "वह है" यह जान लिया — उसको तत्त्व-स्वरूप प्रकट होता है।
verses.commentary: Two-stage knowing. First: 'He is' — bare conviction of existence. Then: the essential nature reveals itself naturally. Faith is the foundation; insight follows.
verses.wordMeaning: Two-stage knowing. First: 'He is' — bare conviction of existence. Then: the essential nature reveals itself naturally. Faith is the foundation; insight follows.

verses.sanskrit: यदा सर्वे प्रमुच्यन्ते कामा येऽस्य हृदि स्थिताः | अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्यत्र ब्रह्म समश्नुते ||
verses.transliteration: yadā sarve pramucyante kāmā ye'sya hṛdi sthitāḥ | atha martyo'mṛto bhavatyatra brahma samaśnute ||
verses.translation: When all the desires settled in his heart are released — then the mortal becomes immortal; here itself he reaches Brahman.
verses.hindi: जब उसके हृदय में स्थित सब कामनाएँ छूट जाती हैं — तब मर्त्य अमर हो जाता है; यहीं वह ब्रह्म को प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: One of the most cited verses. Liberation is not 'after death' — it is in this life, when heart-desires loosen their grip. 'Atra' — 'here.'
verses.wordMeaning: One of the most cited verses. Liberation is not 'after death' — it is in this life, when heart-desires loosen their grip. 'Atra' — 'here.'

verses.sanskrit: यदा सर्वे प्रभिद्यन्ते हृदयस्येह ग्रन्थयः | अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्येतावद्ध्यनुशासनम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā sarve prabhidyante hṛdayasyeha granthayaḥ | atha martyo'mṛto bhavatyetāvaddhyanuśāsanam ||
verses.translation: When all the knots of the heart here below are split open — then the mortal becomes immortal. This much is the instruction.
verses.hindi: जब हृदय की सब ग्रन्थियाँ यहीं छिन्न हो जाती हैं — तब मर्त्य अमर हो जाता है। बस यही उपदेश है।
verses.commentary: The simplest and final formulation: cut the heart-knots — and immortality is here. 'Etāvad anuśāsanam' — 'this much is the teaching.' The whole Upaniṣad in one line.
verses.wordMeaning: The simplest and final formulation: cut the heart-knots — and immortality is here. 'Etāvad anuśāsanam' — 'this much is the teaching.' The whole Upaniṣad in one line.

verses.sanskrit: शतं चैका च हृदयस्य नाड्यस्तासां मूर्धानमभिनिःसृतैका | तयोर्ध्वमायन्नमृतत्वमेति विष्वङ्ङन्या उत्क्रमणे भवन्ति ||
verses.transliteration: śataṃ caikā ca hṛdayasya nāḍyastāsāṃ mūrdhānamabhiniḥsṛtaikā | tayordhvamāyannamṛtatvameti viṣvaṅṅanyā utkramaṇe bhavanti ||
verses.translation: A hundred and one are the nāḍīs of the heart; one of them rises to the crown of the head. By going upward through that, one attains immortality. The others, at the time of departure, go in various directions.
verses.hindi: हृदय की एक सौ एक नाड़ियाँ हैं; उनमें से एक मूर्धा (शिखर) तक जाती है। उसके द्वारा ऊर्ध्व जाने वाला अमरत्व प्राप्त करता है। अन्य नाड़ियाँ — उत्क्रमण के समय — विभिन्न दिशाओं में जाती हैं।
verses.commentary: The yogic anatomy of death. 101 nāḍīs; one (suṣumnā) leads upward through the crown to immortality. Others lead to lower destinations. The teaching of the 'right exit.'
verses.wordMeaning: The yogic anatomy of death. 101 nāḍīs; one (suṣumnā) leads upward through the crown to immortality. Others lead to lower destinations. The teaching of the 'right exit.'

verses.sanskrit: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽन्तरात्मा सदा जनानां हृदये सन्निविष्टः | तं स्वाच्छरीरात् प्रवृहेन्मुञ्जादिवेषीकां धैर्येण | तं विद्याच्छुक्रममृतं तं विद्याच्छुक्रममृतमिति ||
verses.transliteration: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo'ntarātmā sadā janānāṃ hṛdaye sanniviṣṭaḥ | taṃ svāccharīrāt pravṛhenmuñjādiveṣīkāṃ dhairyeṇa | taṃ vidyācchukramamṛtaṃ taṃ vidyācchukramamṛtamiti ||
verses.translation: The Person of the size of a thumb, the inner Self, ever seated in the hearts of people — one should patiently draw him out from one's own body, as one draws the stalk from the muñja grass. Know him as the bright, the immortal — know him as the bright, the immortal.
verses.hindi: अंगुष्ठ-मात्र पुरुष — अन्तरात्मा — सदा जनों के हृदय में बैठा है। उसे अपने शरीर से धैर्य-पूर्वक निकालना चाहिये — जैसे मुञ्ज से ईषीका (अन्दर की पतली डण्ठल) निकाली जाती है। उसे शुक्र, अमर जान — उसे शुक्र, अमर जान।
verses.commentary: The image of separating the inner stalk from the muñja-grass — patient, precise. The Self, like that inner stalk, is to be carefully distinguished from the body. The doubled phrase marks the end.
verses.wordMeaning: The image of separating the inner stalk from the muñja-grass — patient, precise. The Self, like that inner stalk, is to be carefully distinguished from the body. The doubled phrase marks the end.

verses.sanskrit: मृत्युप्रोक्तां नचिकेतोऽथ लब्ध्वा विद्यामेतां योगविधिं च कृत्स्नम् | ब्रह्मप्राप्तो विरजोऽभूद्विमृत्युरन्योऽप्येवं यो विदध्यात्ममेव ||
verses.transliteration: mṛtyuproktāṃ naciketo'tha labdhvā vidyāmetāṃ yogavidhiṃ ca kṛtsnam | brahmaprāpto virajo'bhūdvimṛtyuranyo'pyevaṃ yo vidadhyātmameva ||
verses.translation: Having received this knowledge spoken by Death — and the whole discipline of yoga — Naciketas became free of dust, free of death, attained to Brahman. So shall any other who knows the Self thus.
verses.hindi: मृत्यु-कथित इस विद्या और सम्पूर्ण योग-विधि को प्राप्त करके — नचिकेता ब्रह्म-प्राप्त हुआ, निर्मल हुआ, मृत्यु-रहित हुआ। ऐसे ही जो कोई अन्य भी आत्मा को इस प्रकार जाने — वह भी ऐसा ही होगा।
verses.commentary: The closing verse. The boy who began the journey by asking has now arrived: brahma-prāpta, virajas (dustless), vi-mṛtyu (deathless). And the door is open for any who follow.
verses.wordMeaning: The closing verse. The boy who began the journey by asking has now arrived: brahma-prāpta, virajas (dustless), vi-mṛtyu (deathless). And the door is open for any who follow.

verses.sanskrit: योगश्चित्तवृत्तिरोधो योगो मोक्षप्रदायकः | योगः सर्वबन्धानां योगो आत्मसमाश्रयः ||
verses.transliteration: yogaścittavṛttirodho yogo mokṣapradāyakaḥ | yogaḥ sarvabandhānāṃ yogaḥ ātmasamāśrayaḥ ||
verses.translation: Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications; yoga gives liberation. Yoga cuts all bonds; yoga rests on the Self.
verses.hindi: योग चित्त-वृत्तियों का निरोध है; योग मोक्ष देता है। योग सभी बंधनों को काटता है; योग आत्मा पर आश्रित है।
verses.commentary: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of the Self. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of the Self.
verses.wordMeaning: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of the Self. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of the Self.

verses.sanskrit: अहं ब्रह्मास्मि न त्वं भूतिर्न च भूतानि | सर्वं आत्मा एव सर्वं आत्मा मयि सर्वम् ||
verses.transliteration: ahaṃ brahmāsmi na tvaṃ bhūtirna ca bhūtāni | sarvaṃ ātmā eva sarvaṃ ātmā mayi sarvam ||
verses.translation: I am Brahman, not you; I am birth, not beings; all is Self alone, all is Self in me.
verses.hindi: मैं ब्रह्म हूँ, तुम नहीं; मैं जन्म हूँ, प्राणी नहीं; सब आत्मा ही है, सब आत्मा मेरे में है।
verses.commentary: The declaration of non-duality with the Self as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is Self; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.
verses.wordMeaning: The declaration of non-duality with the Self as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is Self; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.

verses.sanskrit: यथा नदी समुद्रेषु यथा दीपो दीतेषु | तथा जीवो आत्मनि लीनो न तत्र संशयो भवति ||
verses.transliteration: yathā nadī samudreṣu yathā dīpo dīpiteṣu | tathā jīvo ātmani līno na tatra saṃśayo bhavati ||
verses.translation: As rivers merge into the ocean, as lamps merge into light — so the individual self merges into the Self. There is no doubt about this.
verses.hindi: जैसे नदियाँ समुद्र में लीन हो जाती हैं, जैसे दीप ज्योति में लीन हो जाते हैं — वैसे ही जीव आत्मा में लीन हो जाता है। इसमें कोई संशय नहीं।
verses.commentary: The dissolution of individuality into the Self. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.
verses.wordMeaning: The dissolution of individuality into the Self. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.

verses.sanskrit: शान्तं शिवमद्वैतं आत्मा नित्यं शुद्धमच्युतम् | यो जानाति स पश्यति यो न जानाति न पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: śāntaṃ śivamadvaitaṃ ātmā nityaṃ śuddhamacyutam | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Peaceful, auspicious, non-dual Self — eternal, pure, immutable. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: शांत, शिव, अद्वैत आत्मा — नित्य, शुद्ध, अच्युत। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The attributes of the Self: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.
verses.wordMeaning: The attributes of the Self: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.

verses.sanskrit: एको देवो द्वितीयो नास्ति यो आत्मानं वेद तत्त्वतः | सोऽहमस्मि न किंचिद्भूतो न मृत्युर्न शोको न तथा ||
verses.transliteration: eko devo dvitīyo nāsti yo ātmānaṃ veda tattvataḥ | so'hamasmi na kiñcidbhūto na mṛtyurna śoko na tathā ||
verses.translation: There is one God, no second — he who knows the Self in truth. I am He, not any being, no death, no sorrow, and so on.
verses.hindi: एक ही देव है, दूसरा कोई नहीं — जो आत्मा को तत्व से जानता है। मैं वही हूँ, कोई प्राणी नहीं, मृत्यु नहीं, शोक नहीं, वगैरह।
verses.commentary: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.
verses.wordMeaning: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.
